lawyer:
Ranjan Chakravorty, Advocate—For the Petitioners 
Md Mahfuj ul Alam, Advocate—For the Opposite-Party No. 1.
parties:
Sagir Ahmed and others Defendant----- Petitioners
vs
Ataur Rab Chowdhury ------- Plaintiff-Opposite Party
full_judgment:
The Rule issued calling upon the opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 24-2-2011 and 2-3-2011 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Nilphamari in Title Appeal No. 79 of 2001 disallowing the appeal, affirming the judgment and decree dated 23-7-2001 (decree signed on 29-7-2001) passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Domar, Nilphamari in Civil Suit No.1 of 1984 should not be set aside and/or pass such other order or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The facts giving rise to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus: The opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted the original Other Class Suit No.1 of 1984 in the court of the learned Assistant Judge, Domar, Nilphamari for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession contending inter alia that the suit property originally belong to the predecessor of the plaintiff and defendants Nos. 13-21, Monir Uddin Chowdhury. At the demise of Monir Uddin Chowdhury there was an amicable partition among the heirs of Monir Uddin Chowdhury and by virtue of that amicable partition the plaintiff obtained the 'ka' schedule land. The further case of the plaintiff is such that the predecessor of other defendants, namely Siddique Hossen obtained lease from the father of the plaintiff during his life time and while Siddique Hossen stopped in paying the rent, the father of the plaintiff after filing a suit obtained a decree, against which Siddique Hossen ran up to the Honourable Supreme Court of Bangladesh but being failed purchased the land described in schedule 'Ga' of the plaint from other co-sharers. Monir Uddin Chowdhury and one Azizar Rahman subsequently amicably possessed their shares and by way of compromise the plaintiff, exclusively possessed the suit land and in the month of August, 1971 the predecessor of the defendants Siddique Hossen forcibly entered into the 'Ka' schedule land and creating a boundary erected homestead with the help of the then Pakistan Army who had a camp at Chilahati and Siddique Hossen was a member of the then peace committee which was formed by the occupation force Pakistan Army and out of fear at that time, the plaintiff could not give any resistance to Siddique Hossen, the predecessor of the defendants. Subsequently, after the independence of Bangladesh the plaintiff repeatedly requested the defendants to hand over vacant possession of the suit land but the defendants denied. Finding no other alternative, the plaintiff instituted the original suit for confirmation of title and eviction of the defendants from the suit property. 

3. The contrary case of the defendants in short is thus, that the predecessor of the defendants never forcibly entered into the suit property and erected homestead therein and the plaintiff out of ill motive to grab the suit property on false allegation filed the original suit. 

4. The learned trial court during trial of the original suit after framing six different issues decided all the issues in favour of the plaintiff and decreed the suit on contest by its judgment and decree dated 23-6-1987.

5. Being aggrieved the defendants preferred an appeal being Title Appeal No. 79 of 2001 in the court of the learned District Judge, Nilphamari, which was transmitted to the court of the learned Joint District Judge, Nilphamari for hearing and disposal and the learned appellate court on hearing the appeal by the impugned judgment and decree dated 24-2-2011 disallowed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. 

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree the defendant-appellant-petitioners have preferred this civil revision under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule with an interim order of stay and status quo. 

7. During hearing of the Rule Mr Ranjan Chakravorty, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the petitioners while Mr Md Mahfuj ul Alam the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the opposite party No. 1. 

8. Mr Ranjan Chakravorty, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that, admittedly the suit property originally belonged to Monir Uddin Chowdhury the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiff. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned trial court as well as the appellate court during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal failed to appreciate that the 'ka' schedule property which consists of 05 decimals of land, was ascertained by a civil court commissioner and that land is under the exclusive possession of the defendants and prior to them, their predecessor Siddique Hossen. The learned Advocate also submits that it is the positive case of the defendants that initially Siddique Hossen was a permissive possessor under the plaintiff's predecessor, Moinuddin Ahmed and since that permissive possession the defendants are possessing the suit property. Subsequently, by two registered sub-kabala deed dated 21-12-1967 and 18-4-1968 the predecessor of the defendant-petitioners Siddique Hossen purchased the 'Ga' schedule property and that the petitioner's predecessor Siddique Hossen and after his death the present petitioners are not the trespassers to the suit land, and Siddique Hossen was not a member of peace committee in the year 1971 and not dispossessed the plaintiff or his predecessor with the help of Pakistan Army and the plaintiff to the suit Motlob Hossen Chowdhury inasmuch as not corroborated his plaint case, the case of the plaintiff is not proved but the learned trial court as well as the appellate court being guided by surmise and conjecture decided the merit of the suit and the subsequent appeal infavour of the plaintiff and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree deserve interference of this court. 

9. As against the aforesaid submission of the learned Counsel for the petitioners, the learned Counsel .appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-opposite party controverting the argument advanced from the side of the learned Counsel for the petitioners submits that, the trial court as well as the appellate court during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal committed no illegality or irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that, admittedly the suit property belonged to the predecessor of the plaintiff, Monir Uddin Chowdhury and in support of the plaintiff's case he has filed the 'bontonnama' by virtue of which the suit property was devolved upon the exclusive possession and title of Monir Uddin Chowdhury. The learned Advocate further submits that the Advocate Commissioner's report which has been marked as Exhibit-'7' has specified the suit property and the concerned CS khatian vide Exhibit-1, it's map vide Exhibit-2, conclusively proved that the contention of the plaintiff is supported by tangible documentary evidence and on the other hand, the defendants by adducing any cogent evidence measurably have failed to prove that their predecessor Siddique Hossen was in possession of the suit property by way of getting permission from the plaintiff's predecessor Monir Uddin Chowdhury. The learned Advocate also submits that the defendants have also failed to produce any paper which can be treated authentic in support of the defendant's case and since the plaintiff to the suit at the relevant time was very much sick and was not able to move his normal pursuit. PW 1 Monjurul Hoque Chowdhury on behalf of the plaintiff, who happens to be a close relative of the plaintiff gave his testimony supporting the pleadings of the plaintiff. The learned Advocate argued that the plaintiff who is the uncle and father-in-law of PW 1 requested him (PW 1) to depose in the court and accordingly, PW 1with the permission of the court made his deposition and he has been thoroughly cross-examined from the side of the defendants and there is no objection at the relevant time from the side of the defendants as to the authority of PW 1, even if; no objection was raised in proving the documents of the plaintiff before the court at the time of trial and in this context the learned counsel referred a decision of our Apex Court reported in 62 DLR (AD) 242 with regard to concurrent observation and findings of the courts below in connection with the right, title, interest, possession and dispossession etc. of the plaintiff to the suit land. The learned Advocate lastly submits that there is no misreading or non-reading of evidence and non consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice from the side of the learned appellate court by which the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with. 

10. In order to appreciate the submission advanced from the sides of the learned counsels for the parties, having gone through the pleadings of the parties, the judgment and decree passed by the learned trial court in Other Suit No. 01 of 1984, the judgment and decree passed by the appellate court in Title Appeal No. 79 of 2001, the evidence led from the sides of the respective parties and the documents produced with all other connected papers it transpires that it is an admitted position that the suit property appertaining to mouza Veladaburi under Domar Upozilla corresponding to CS Khatian No. 428 and subsequent RS khatian No. 564, Plot No. 8370 consists of 10 decimals of land, out of which 05 decimals of land originally belonged to the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiff and the defendants No. 13-21 namely Monir Uddin Chowdhury. It is the specific contention of the plaintiff that after the death of Monir Uddin Chowdhury the legal heirs entered in to an amicable partition and by way of that partition the suit land had been owning and possessing by the plaintiff. It is the pleading's case of the plaintiff that the plaintiff's father Monir Uddin Chowdhury during his life time rented the suit land in favour of the original defendant's predecessor Md Siddique and at the refusal to pay the rent Monir Uddin Chowdhury obtained a decree against the predecessor of the defendants and by way of execution of that decree the predecessor of the plaintiff realized the arear rents from Siddique Hossen. 

11. The contrary case as it appears from the contesting defendant's pleadings is such that, initially the predecessor of the defendants was a permissive possessor under Monir Uddin Chowdhury and subsequently, after getting registered kabala deeds in respect of other lands from the co-sharers of the CS recorded tenants possessed the suit property openly and adversely against the owner of the property. 

12. In order to substantiate the respective cases of the parties, they have adduced oral evidences and besides this, the plaintiff has submitted his basic documents, which are the C.S. khatian. No. 428 and its map marked as Exhibit-'1 &2', the certified copy of the Money Suit No. 53 of 1959 (Exhibit-3) its decree (Exhibit -4) and the certified copy of the judgment and decree passed in Money Appeal No. 10 of 1963 [Exhibit-4-(ka)1, the certified copy of the Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No. 94-D of 1966 (Exhibit-5), the papers relating to amicable partition [Exhibit-6 & 6-(ka)1 and the photocopy of Civil Courts Commissioner's Report [Exhibit -7-(ka)1. 

13. Apart from this, PW 1 Monjurul Hoque Chowdhury, who is the son-in-law of the plaintiff, in his testimony testified that his uncle as well as father-in-law is sick having pain in his waist and that is why he is giving deposition on behalf of his father-in-law. P.W. 1 in his examination-in-chief, specifically corroborated the plaint case and during his cross-examination in a reply to a question from the side of the defendants this witness categorically testified that during the war of liberation in the year 1971 AD the predecessor of the defendants, Siddique Mia dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit property, who was a member of peace committee. PW 2 AKM Zakaira Bosunia in his testimony testified that, he knows the parties and the suit land and the plaintiff has been dispossessed from the suit land by the defendants in the month of August, 1971 and the suit land is 05 decimals, arise out of Plot No. 8370. During cross examination in a reply to a question from the side of the defendants, PW 2 testifies that after 25th March of 1971, he was at Chilahati and the Pakistan Army had a camp there. In another stage of cross-examination, PW 2 categorically testifies that Siddique Miah with the help of other non-bengali including one Lutfor dispossessed the plaintiff 'and after dispossession the suit land has been 'gheraoed' by "chagar". The Civil Court Commissioner Md Asaduzzaman Miah has been deposed as court witness and this witness in his disposition testifies that due to missing of the original copy, he has produced the photocopy of the report. This witness has identified the photocopy which has been marked as Exhibit -7 (ka) as secondary evidence by the learned trial court. 

14. Vis-a-vis, the defendant No. 1 Sagir Ahmed as DW 1 testified before the court and during his testimony he has categorically testifies that he is deposing on behalf of defendants Nos. 1-11 and the owner of the suit land was Monir Uddin Chowdhury and Hazi Azizar Rahman and by amicable arrangement the suit land has been devolved upon Monir Uddin Chowdhury and his father Siddique Miah for the sake of his business on the basis of permission from Monir Uddin Chowdhury started to reside in the suit land. D.W. 1 further admitted in his testimony that treating Siddique Miah a "varatia", Monir Uddin Chowdhury owned the case and subsequently by way of decree execution, he has realized the decreetal amount. DW 1 further testified that, prior to this suit they have purchased the 'Gha' schedule land. 

15. During cross-examination from the side of the plaintiff, DW 1 testified at a stage that the son-in-law of the plaintiff, Monjurul Hoque Chowdhury created a false field 'porcha' in the name of Mosjid committee out of the land of their Plot No. 8369. In a reply to a question D.W.1 conceded that his father is non-bengali and Moslemuddin is the eldest son of Monir Uddin Chowdhury. DW 1 (the defendant No. 1) during his cross-examination frankly admitted at a stage that they have purchased no land from the suit Plot No. 8370. The witness No.2 of the defendants during his testimony testified that he knows the parties and the suit land and that land consists of Plot No. 8369 and 8365 and he does not know as to whether there is any plot other than these two plots in the suit property. This witness in his deposition testified about the possession of the defendants. DW 3 Mossarraf Hossen in his testimony testifies that the land of Plot No. 8370 is being possessed by the defendants along with one Fazlul Hoque & a mosque, and in the last sentence of his examination-in-chief. D.W. 3 Mosarraf Hossain testifies "বিবাদীরা কোন জমি জোরপূর্বক দখল করে নাই। ব্রিটিশ আমল থেকে বাদীর দখলে আছে।" During cross-examination this witness testified that the defendants have dwelling but n Plot No. 8369 and 8365 and the suit Plots are 8369 and 8365 and besides this, there is no suit plot. The last witness of the defendants, DW 4 Md Toimur Rahman in his deposition testified that the defendants are in possession over the suit homestead and the suit land is 8369 and 8365 and in the year 1971, the defendants did not dispossess the plaintiff from the suit land. 

16. On meticulous consideration of the evidence on records, I have the reason to incline such a view that the witnesses adduced from the side of the plaintiff are mere competent and trustworthy with regard to the defendant's witnesses. The plaintiff's witnesses have been thoroughly cross-examined from the side of the defendants, but their evidence appears to be sound and cogent and on the contrary, the evidentiary value of the defendant's witnesses are nil inasmuch as, their testimonies are full of ambiguity, discrepancy as well as inconsistencies and contradictory with the pleadings of the defendants. The learned trial court as well as the appellate court concurrently in their observation and findings rightly after proper appreciation of law and apprising evidences on records in its true perspective arrived at a conclusive decision that the plaintiff's case has been proved and there is no misreading and non-reading of evidence or non consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice from the side of the learned appellate court by dint of which the impugned judgment and decree can be interfered with invoking section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

17. It is a decided matter in our judicature that the findings of facts as decided by the appellate court being the final court of facts are immune from interference in absence of the aforesaid illegalities. [Ref: Abdul Gofitr vs Md Abdur Razzak 62 DLR (AD) 242; All vs Joynul Abedin, 35 DLR (AD) 216; Government of Bangladesh vs A KM Abdul Hai 9 MLR (AD) 82 & 56 DLR (AD) 53 = 56 DLR (AD) 53]. 

18. In the instant case, since the defendants have a definite case as to their alleged permissive possession from the admitted owner Monir Uddin Chowdhury under the ambit of section 103 of the Evidence Act 1872, it is the incumbent duty upon the defendants to prove that, but the facts remain that the defendants have miserably failed to discharge their onus of proof by producing any tangible evidence, either oral or documentary, which can be treated trustworthy in believing their alleged permissive possession from the predecessor of the plaintiff. Apart from this, if it is proved for .argument sake, nevertheless no adverse possession accrued under the law of adverse possession, which is initiated on the basis of permission to possess the land. 

19. Having regard to the facts, circumstances and the discussions referred to above I am constrained to hold such a view that the Rule has got no merit to succeed. 

20. In the result; the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 24-2-2011 and 2-3-2011 respectively passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Nilphamari in Title Appeal No. 79 of 2001 disallowing the appeal affirming the judgment and decree dated 23-7-2001 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Domar, Nilphamari in Title Suit No.1 of 1984 is hereby affirmed. 

21. The order of stay & status quo granted earlier at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacated. 

22. Communicate the judgment and order at once. 

Send down the Lower Court's Records immediately. 

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.4766 of 2017
lawyer:
Mr. A. B. Roy Chowdhury, Advocate instructed by Syed Mahbubar Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioners

Mr Kamal Ul Alam, Senior Advocate instructed by Mr. Zainul Abedin, Advocate-on-Record ----- For Respondent No.3

For Respondent Nos.1-2, 4-6 ----- None represented
parties:
Nikhil Kanti Chowdhury and others -------- Petitioners

-Vs-

Pronab Kumar Chakraborty and others ---------- Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 7th day of August, 2017 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.4088 of 2000)
full_judgment:
Abu Bakar Siddiquee J. This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated the 7th day of August, 2017 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.4088 of 2000 discharging the Rule.

2. The facts, relevant for disposal of this petition, are that the predecessor-in-interest of present petitioner Nos.1-4 as plain-tiff instituted Partition Suit No.131 of 1978 in the Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 3rd Court, Chittagong for partition. Subsequently, the suit was transferred to the Court of Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Sadar, Chittagong and was re-numbered as Partition Suit No.149 of 1984. Thereafter, the suit was again transferred to the Court of Assistant Judge, Additional Court No.3, Chittagong and was re-numbered as Partition Suit No.25 of 1990.

3. The case of the plaintiff is that the disputed property described in schedule No.1 to the plaint originally belonged to one Moumohan Durtta. At the demise of Monmohan Dutta, his only son Nogendra Lal Dutta and wife, Tarangini Dutta succeeded him. RS Khatian was correctly prepared and published in their names. Tarangini Dutta in 1963 filed Partition Suit No.10 of 1963 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Chittagong against her son, Nogendra Lal Dutta. The suit was decreed with cost. Tarangini filed Decree Execution Case No.13 of 1967 against Nogendra Lal Dutta and the execution case was satisfied by auction sale of the suit land described in schedule No.2 and the property was auction purchased by Satish Chandra Chakraborty, predecessor-in-interest of respondent No.6 and Borjendra Lal Chowdhury, predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners. Satish Chandra Chowdhury committed fraud in the process of delivery of possession in the manner that the process surveyor gave possession of .02 acres land to the petitioners' predecessor-in-interest and .09 acres to Satish Chandra Chakraborty. But the petitioners have been possessing the suit land in equal share in ejmali. The petitioners are in possession in the suit land by erecting dwelling houses, but the defendants are trying to possess more than their share because of the fraudulent return of the decree execution case. The plaintiff (now dead) in the last part of August, 1978 requested the respondents for amicable partition of the suit land but failed; hence this suit.

4. Defendant Nos.1 and 6 contested the suit by filing two separate written statements denying the material allegations contending, inter alia, that the suit is not properly valued and duly stamped. The suit is barred by limitation. The plaintiffs cannot get any relief in this suit except by a separate suit for declaration of title and partition. The suit is barred under the principle of waiver, acquiescence and estoppel and is not maintainable in its present form.

5. Defendant No.6 in her own motion got herself added a party in the suit and filed a separate written statement endorsing the case of defendant No.1 (now deceased) specifically contending that on 01.02.1980, she purchased .0150 acres land from defendant No.1 and she is living in the suit land by erecting dwelling houses. Defendant No.1 purchassed the suit land in auction in his name of the his own funds but fraudulently the plaintiff being his Karjakarak inserted his name in boynama and the fact of such fraud has been disclosed at the time of taking delivery of possession and upon the request of the plaintiff, he was allotted one gonda share for the purpose of erecting a dwelling hut. Excepting such portion of land the suit is liable to be dismissed.

6. During trial, both the parties adduced and produced the oral and documentary evidence.

7. The trial Court dismissed the suit holding that a simple suit for partition is not maintainable since the plaintiff failed to prove his right, title, interest and possession over the entire land in suit as has been claimed by him.

8. Against the said judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiff preferred Other Appeal No.380 of 1990 before the learned District Judge, Chittagong. The appeal was transmitted to the Court of Additional District Judge, 4th Court, Chittagong. The learned Additional District Judge disallowed the appeal affirming those of the trial Court.

9. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court below, the successors of the plaintiff filed Civil Revision No.4088 of 2000 before the High Court Division. The learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division discharged the Rule.

10. Against the judgment and order of the High Court Division, the successors of the plaintiff filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.4766 of 2017 before this Division seeking leave.

11. Mr. A. B. Roy Chowdhury, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioners, submits that the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division acted illegally and without considering the evidence on record discharged the Rule and that the petitioners are in possession of the suit land which has been proved by sufficient evidence. He further submits that the High Court Division failed to consider that the defendants totally failed to prove their title and possession by producing oral and documentary evidence and that the High Court Division failed to consider the scope of rule 95 of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure which contemplates the eviction of the judgment-debtor and put the auction purchaser into possession and that there is nothing to effect partition for such auction purchased property, but all the Courts below including the High Court Division remained silent about the said fact. He further submits that the case of the petitioners is that exhibit No.' E' is a collusive document used by defendant No.1 and the same was not sustainable by the document itself as it was not signed by the Advocates of the parties and the High Court Division is totally wrong in not coining into definite findings on this point. He lastly submits that the Courts below and the High Court Division did not- consider that the possession is always delivered in accordance with sale certificate because the same is put into execution and presumption goes that the decree-holder auction purchased the suit property in equal share.

12. Mr. Kamal Ul Alam, learned Senior Advocate, appearing for respondent No.3 supported the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division, but none appeared on behalf other respondents. He argued that as per his own admission, the plaintiff is entitled to a saham for one gonda land in dispute. Fie adds that the S.A. and the R.S. record have been prepared in the name of the defendant long ago, but the plaintiff had not tried to get the same recorded in his name and as such, the simple suit for partition is not maintainable.

13. We have heard the learned Advocates for both the parties and perused the materials on record.

14. The suit land originally belonged to one Monmohon Dutta who died leaving behind only son named Nogendra Lal Dutta and a wife named Tarongini Dutta. It is also admitted that Taronginu Dutta filed Partition Suit No.10 of 1963 and obtained decree with cost and for recovery of cost, she filed and Execution Case No.13 of 1967 and that the plaintiff (predecessor of the present petitioners) and defendant No.1 purchased the suit property in auction to the extent of the portion of Nogendra Lal Dutta.

15. The plaintiff (predecessor of the petitioners) has come with an allegation that the auction purchased property was never partitioned by metes and bounds between them and the plaintiff asked for effecting partition but defendant No.1 denied.

16. On the other hand, the contesting defendants denied the claim of the plain-tiff and counter claimed that the plaintiff was the servant and tadbirkar of defendant No.1 who was entrusted with a task of purchasing the said property in auction and he collusively created boinama inserting his name along with the name of defendant No.1 showing himself to have purchased the same in equal share. It has been further alleged that subsequently, the alleged fact of collusion was disclosed and the plaintiff begged pardon to defendant No.1 and prayed for allocation of one gonda of land in his favour for the purpose of erecting his dwelling hut. It has been further alleged that upon such prayer, defendant No.1 allocated only one gonda land in the suit holding but suppressing this fact, the plaintiff instituted this partition suit claiming half portion of the land in suit with a view to grab the property of the defendant.

17. The trial Court during trial of the original suit after examining two witnesses from the side of the plaintiff and 03 witnesses from the side of the defendants, on perusal of the evidence produced therein and evaluation of the same, dismissed the suit on contest by his judgment and decree dated 31.05.1990 which has been affirmed by the appellate Court as well as the Single Bench of the High Court Division.

 

18. From the testimony of the plaintiff, it is apparent that the plaintiff admitted in course of his examination-in-chief that pursuant to the auction dated 19.02.1968, he went into possession through Court. It further appears that the plaintiff asserts that in the last part of August, 1978, the defendants tried to construct a house in the vacant land and in spite of his protest, the defendants have erected two houses there-in. PW1 during his deposition in reply to a question from the side of the defendants admits that defendant No.1 dispossessed him after institution of the suit from the vacant land and he further admits that no amendment was sought for to that effect by him and it was not even informed to the trial Court. The plaintiff stated during the course of his deposition that against the B.S khatian, he lodged objection, but his objection has been rejected. At a stage of his testimony, the plaintiff admits that pursuant to the final order passed in Execution Case No.13 of 1967 (exhibit-'D') they filed an application for possession and the certified copy of that application has been identified by the plaintiff Brojendra Lai. On the basis of his admission, it was marked as exhibit-E. It appears that PW 1 deposed that in the year 1968, he was a clerk of an Advocate, namely, Umesh Chandra Chowdhury, and at -the time of giving deposition, he is also working as an Advocate's clerk of Advocate Bisheshor. The plaintiff deposed before the Court that after such taking over the possession, he took no step nor filed any case in any Court against the same.

19. Now the plaintiff filed this partition suit praying for effecting partition to the extent of half portion of the auction purchased property. It was finally disposed of in Execution Case No.13 of 1967 on 01.04.1968 A.D. The boinama of the auction sale stands in the names of the plain-tiff and defendant No.1 in equal share. But in this regard, it is the definite contention of the defendant that the plaintiff was the Tadbirkar of defendant No.1 who was entrusted with the task of purchasing the property in auction in favour of defendant No.1 and taking advantage of that, the plaintiff managed to have his name inserted as one of the purchasers with defendant No.1 in the boinama which has been marked as Exhibit-' A'. The fact remains that, pursuant to boinama there was delivery of possession and prior to that, admittedly the auction purchaser, defendant No.1 along with the plaintiff jointly filed an application on 05.03.1968 in the 3rd Court of the then Sub-ordinate Judge, Chattogram under Order XXI, rule 95 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The plaintiff as PW1 admitted in the said application before the concerned Court in connection with the auction purchase. In that application, there is a recital, which reads as follows:

আমরা ১/২ নিলাম খরিদ্দার প্রার্থিকগণ দাইকের নিম্ন তপশিলের স্থাবর সম্পত্তি ১০/০১/৬৮ ইংরেজী তারিখে আদালতে প্রকাশ্য নিলামে নিম্ন লিখিত মতে খরিদ করিয়া বয়নামা প্রাপ্তি মালীক হইয়াছি। আমরা প্রার্থিকার তপশিলের জমি নিম্ন লিখিত মতে দখল পাওয়া আবশ্যক ।

 অতএব প্রার্থনা যে, নিম্ন তপসিলের দাইকের স্বতীয় সম্পত্তি নিম্ন লিখিত মতে আইনতঃ ২১ অর্ডার ৯৫ রুল মতে দখল দেওয়ার আদেশ হয় । ইতি-

তপশীল

১। মৌজে মাদার বাড়ী খানা ডবলমুরিং মহল ১৪৬৯৮ নং হাল ৯৬০৫ জিং কিমাং কাঠা ও ৩৪২৪ নং জিং বদু ও আর.এস জরিপের ৪8৪৯ নং খতিয়ানের ৩০৬৪ দাগের ও আর.এস জরিপের ৫১৫ নং খতিয়ানের ৩০৬৪৩২৫৭ দাগের আং পি.এস জরিপের ১৬১৪ নং খতিয়ানের ৩৪৮৫ দাগের ও ১৬১৩ নং খতিয়ানের পি.এস ৩৪৮৬ দাগের আর.এস ও পি.এস উভয়ের দাগের ৫।। কড়া জমির মধ্যে আমি ২নং নিলাম খরিদ্দার প্রার্থীকের আমরা ১/২ নং প্রার্থিক নিলাম খরিদ্দারের আপোষ মতে আমি ২নং প্রার্থীকের সর্ব দক্ষিণে চলাচল রাস্তার সংলগ্ন ১ এক গন্ডা তৎ উত্তরে আমি ১নং প্রার্থিক নিলাম খরিদ্দারের অবশিষ্ট ৪।। চারিগন্ডা দুই কড়া সর্ব মোট ৫।। পচ গা দুই কড়া জমি।

20. The certified copy of this application which is an attested document from both the parties has been marked as Exhibit-"E'. Therein, the plaintiff appears to have prayed for only one gonda of land. Pursuant to that application, the concerned Court vide his order dated 01.04.1968 passed an order and in compliance of that order, the process server delivered possession. All these papers have been duly proved and after admission from the side of the plaintiff those have been exhibited. In this context, it is required to be mentioned that the plaintiff to the suit is an Advocate's Mohorar who is supposed to be a well acquainted person having knowledge about auction and its subsequent proceedings upto the final order passed by the executing Court.

21. The learned Judges of the Courts below after proper assessment of the relevant evidence on records and appreciation of law arrived at a concurrent decision that the claim of the plaintiff-petitioner to the extent of 50% of the auctioned property is barred, inasmuch as he is estopped by law from claiming the suit property as prayed for in the schedule of the plaint.

22. Sections 20 and 21 of the Evidence Act, 1872 provides admission by persons expressly referred to by party to suit and proof of admissions, against persons making them, and by or on their behalf Our Apex Court in the case of Hajee Abdus Sattar-Vs-Mahiuddin and others, VI BLD (AD)224, opined admission between the parties made in another proceeding-respondent's admission that he was a ten-ant under the appellant estopped him from denying appellants' title in the suit premises. Admission by way of statements made in documents certified to be true copies by an authorized officer of the Government arc admissible in evidence and the plain-tiff having stated in Exhibit-T' that he would take one gonda on the south and defendant No.1 would get the rest of the auctioned property, he cannot now claim half of the suit land.

23. In the case of Birendra Chandra Saha-Vs-Sashi Mohan Saha, 27 DLR (SC)89, it was decided by their lordships that, admission is a substantive piece of evidence.

24. Having considered those facts, circumstances and evidence on record, all the Courts below have come to a concurrent finding that the plaintiff prayed for delivery of the possession for one gonda of land and the same has been possessed by him as his own homestead.

25. On perusal of the record, it appears that the SA and the RS record have been prepared in the name of defendant and the defendant has been paying rents for the same since long, whereas the plaintiff sought for simple partition without seeking any relief of declaration of title. Thus it appears that the very framing of the suit is defective. All the Courts below have concurrently arrived at a decision that as per petition under Order XXI, rule 95 of the CPC, the plaintiff is entitled to get a saham to the extent of one gonda share as per aforementioned petition under Order XXI, rule 95 of the C.P.C. On the other hand, the defendant will get the rest of the land contained in the schedule of the boinama which appears to be four gonda and two kora. DW 1, Pranab Kumar Chakraborty, is the son of Shatish Chakraborty (who purchased the suit land in auction) as DW1 deposed that Brojen Babu was their Clerk who was entrusted with the task of purchasing the land in auction, but he by committing breach of trust inserted his name in the boinama in a fraudulent manner and such an act of concoction has been divulged subsequently. He further stated in his evidence that Brojen Babu begged pardon and prayed for allocating one gonda land in the suit jote for the purpose of erecting a dwelling house and upon such prayer a joint petition (Exhibit-E) under Order XXI, rule 95 of the Civil Procedure Code was filed before the executing Court for the purpose of delivering possession and accordingly possession was delivered in their favour. He also adds that since then they have been possessing 4 gondas 2 koras of land and defendant has been possessing one gonda of land. DW2 Krion Shankar Chakraborty deposed that both the parties have been possessing the suit land as per saham which has been allocated through delivery of possession. DW3 also deposed that the plaintiffs have been possessing only one gonda share in the suit jote. Thus, it appears that all the DWs have corroborated each other in this respect. And as such, we find that nothing cogent could be elicited to disbelieve them. All the Courts below upon sifting those evidence came to a concurrent finding that the plaintiff has been possessing only one gonda share in the suit jote as per condition laid down in the petition filed under Order XXI, rule 95 of Code of Civil Procedure. We, thus, find no option but to advert such a concurrent find of fact since there is no misreading and non-consideration as well as mis-appreciation of evidence.

26. Since the plaintiff and in his place the petitioners admittedly, own one gonda of land in the suit jote, so he is to get saham for the same.

27. Accordingly the leave petition is disposed off.

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 22nd day of July, 2010 passed by the High Court Division in First. Appeal (FA) No.286 of 2008)
full_judgment:
Abu Bakar Siddiquee, J: This civil appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgement and order dated the 22nd day of July, 2010 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal (FA) No.286 of 2008 allowing the appeal. 

2. The facts relevant to dispose of the case are that the appellant as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No.78 of 2006 in the Court of the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Sylhet (in-charge) for partition of the suit property as described in the plaint stating, inter alia, that the suit land belonged to one Hakim Boshirul Haque Chowdhury, who, continuance of his possession in the land, died leaving behind six sons including the plaintiff-appellant, two daughters and wife-Sabera Khanam. Later on, his daughter-Saleha Khanam and wife-Sabera Khanam died leaving behind the rest heirs of deceased-Hakim Boshirul Haque Chowdhury. For the convenience of enjoyment of the suit property, all the co-sharers being agreed to effect a partition of the suit property and executed a declaration dated 13-12-2004 (Shoronlipi), on the basis of which the suit land was divided into nine separate and specific saham. Defendant No.1 got 0.0171 acre land at the eastern side, who thereafter constructed a pucca house thereon. In this backdrop, on 20-2-2006, all the co-sharers asked defendant No.1 to execute a partition deed as per their decision and declaration held on 13-12-2004, but on various pretext, the defendant refused to do so and hence the suit. 

3. Defendant Nos. 1, 2-7 and 9 contested the suit by filing two separate written statements denying all the material allegations made in the plaint, contending, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and manner as the suit is barred by law of limitation and all the suit properties were not brought into the hotchpotch. The suit is also bad for defect of the parties and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

4. Upon hearing the parties and on consideration of the materials on record, the learned Joint District Judge, Sylhet by his judgment and decree dated 6-8-2008 decreed the suit. 

5. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree passed by the learned Joint District Judge, defendant No.1 preferred First Appeal No.286 of 2008 before the High Court Division. The learned Judges of the High Court Division allowed the appeal and set-aside the judgment and decree passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Sylhet and sent the suit on remand to the trial Court for fresh trial. 

6. Against the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division, the plaintiff filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1199 of 2011 before this Division and leave was granted to consider the following submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner: 
"Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the petitioner took us through the impugned judgment and papers on record, and submitted that by the admitted declaration or Shoronlipi dated 13-12-2004 the suit land in question has been partitioned amicably by allotting specific saham and specific area, therefore, in case of inclusion of any other land in hotchpotch or schedule of the plaint, the area of the saham as already allotted by mutual agreement or consent would have not been changed in any way." 

7. Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the appellant, submits that the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is misconceived, bad in fact and law. He further submits that the High Court Division committed gross error of law in not considering the fact that the partial partition permissible without prejudicing the parties concerned as has been decided in the case of Nurul Afsar vs Rafiqul Ahmed, reported in 51 DLR (AD) 155. He further submits that admittedly, respondent No.1 alone is in possession of the suit property and prolongation of his possession in the suit property, he denied partition as per their consent declaration or Shoronlipi. He further submits that the High Court Division ought to have held that in case of non-inclusion of entire properties left by Hakim Bashirul Haque Chowdhary, there is nothing to prejudice on the 'part of the parties concerned since they have already agreed to make partition of the scheduled land as appended in the plaint on executing the Shoronlipi dated 13-12-2004. 

8. Mr Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, learned Advocate-on-Record, appearing for respondent Nos. l (f-h) made submissions in support of the impugned judgement and order of the High Court Division. He adds that in this partition suit, there is defect of hotchpot since all the properties left by Hakim Bashirul Haque Chowdhury has not been brought in the schedule of the plaint and, as such, the defendant-respondent are being seriously prejudiced. He also adds that this case is also bad for defect of parties. He finally submits that since the property in dispute has already been partitioned through a registered deed of declaration and, as such, there is no necessity to file this partition suit in the Court. 

9. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for the parties concerned, perused the impugned judgement and order of the High Court Division and other relevant papers on record. 

10. It is admitted by the parties that one Hakim Bashirul Haque Chowdhury was the owner in possession of this suit property who acquired the same by way of purchase and accordingly, the same has been recorded in his name during the course of SA operation. It is also an admitted fact that aforesaid Hakim Bashirul Haque Chowdhury died leaving behind six sons, the plaintiff and defendant Nos. 1-5, two daughters, defendant No.6 and one Saleha Khanum and a wife-Sabera Khanum. It is also admitted by the parties that Saleha Khanum and Sabera Khanum died leaving behind rest heirs of Hakim Bashirul Haque. 

11. The plaintiff has come with an allegation that the heirs of deceased Hakim Bashirul Haque Chowdhury used to live in different places both in home and abroad and some of them are being resided in the suit house standing on this suit land and also that for the convenience of enjoyment of the suit property, all the co-shares agreed to make partition of the land and building and accordingly executed and registered a deed of declaration dated 13-12-2004 and on the basis of which the disputed property was divided in to nine separate saham. It has been further alleged that on 20-2-2006, the plaintiff (petitioner) asked the defendant to execute a partition deed, but defendant No. 1 refused such proposal. 

12. One the other hand, the contesting defendant denied the aforesaid allegation of the plaintiff (petitioner) and counter claimed that as per paras 6 and 7 of the declaration all the properties of the parties have not been included in the schedule of the plaint and, as such, the suit is bad for defect of hotchpotch and thus, the suit is not maintainable which is liable to be dismissed. Defendant Nos. 2-7/9 contended that the suit is bad for defect of parties. It has been further alleged that after the death of Hakim Bashirul Haque Chowdhury, his heirs decided to make partition of the suit land and accordingly, on 13-12-2004 executed a declaration in respect of the suit land and building standing thereon in which the respective share of the parties has been allocated and it was also decided that the cosharers would effect partition of the suit land as per the declaration within 1 year from its execution. But unfortunately, defendant No.1 did not comply with the terms and conditions of the declaration. 

13. We have perused the deed of declaration dated 13-12-2004 (Exhibit-2). 

14. From which it appears that the suit land and the building standing thereon have been divided into several parts and those have been allocated among the co-sharers of the property appended in the schedule of the plaint. PW 1, DWs 1 and 2 are the heirs of Hakini Bashirul Haque Chowdhury who have admitted in their deposition and cross-examination that the said deed of declaration was being executed and registered among them. They have also conceded that they have no objection if the suit land and building standing thereon would be partitioned on basis of deed of declaration. The other defendants, i.e. defendant Nos.2-7/9 agreed to effect partition according to the claim of the plaintiff and they have claimed separate saham in respect of their legitimate' portion of property. The only objection raised by the defendant is that all the properties of the deceased Bashirul Haque Chowdhury have not been brought into the hotchpotch and, as such, the suit is not maintainable in its present from. In this regard, the trial Court decided that though all the properties of the deceased 13shirul Haque Chowdhury have not been brought into hotchpotch, the suit land and the building standing thereon can be made partitioned separately among the co-sharers on the basis of the deed of declaration dated 13-12-2004 since the same has been executed by them on the basis of mutual understanding and considering the convenience and inconvenience among them. Having considered the claim and counter-claim of the parties, we are to ascertain as to whether the partial partition is possible only for the suit land as has been decided by the learned Judge of the trial Court. It appears that respondent No.1 alone is in the possession of the suit property and with a view to maintain and prolongation of his possession in the suit property, he denied partition as per their admitted declaration or shoronlipi. 

15. The learned Judge of the High Court Division held that it is not possible to make partial partition since it is admitted by the parties that part of joint property left by the original owner retaining out of partition and with this end in view, the appellate Court sent back the suit to the trial Court on remand for holding the trial afresh. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant vehemently argued that the High Court Division committed gross error of law in not considering the fact: that partial partition is permissible without prejudicing the parties concerned as has been decided the in the case of Nurul Afrar vs Rafiqul Ahmed reported in Si DLR (AD) 155. In para 7 of such case, it has been held that:- 
"The general rule that a partition suit should embrace all the joint properties of the parties concerned is indeed a rule of convenience. If properties are `left out in a partition suit it brooks further litigation. It is true that this rule is relaxable. But there are specific situations calling for relaxation. They are generally (a) where different portions of the property lie in different jurisdictions or (b) when some portion of the property is at the time incapable of partition or (c) when the property from its nature is impartible, or (d) when property is held jointly with strangers who cannot be joined as parties to a general suit for partition, or (e) where cotenants, by mutual agreement, decide to make partition of a part of the joint property retaining the rest in common.
 
16. From the above decision, it appears that one of the specific situations which make the partial partition possible is item No.(e) of the decision wherein it has been specified to the effect that where the parties in suit decided to make partition of a part of the joint properties by mutual agreement. In the instant case, we find that the heirs of Hakim Bashirullah Chowdhury were being mutually agreed to effect partition through a registered instrument (shoronlipi dated 13-12-2004). Thus, we find that there is no bar to effect partial partition of the land left by Hakim Bashirul Haque among his heirs and thereby set apart the saham of specific area for each of the saham seeker. Therefore, in case of non-inclusion of any other land left by original owner in the schedule of the plaint will not affect nature and maintainability of present partition suit. A partition suit is a suit of recurring cause of action and such the parties may be s, go for further partition for such rest land left by Hakim Bashirul Haque Chowdhury specially in those cases which has been identified in the aforesaid enunciation reported in 51 DLR (AD) page 155, We also observed that there is nothing to prejudice on the part of the parties since they have consented to make partition earlier on executing the shoronlipi. 

17. Since further partition is possible for the rest joint property which has been left out from this case on showing of recurring cause of action, the appellate Court has arrived at a wrong decision of sending in the case to the lower Court on remand for holding trial afresh. Thus, the impugned judgment and decree of the appellate Court below is liable to be set-aside. 

18. Hence, the appeal is liable to be allowed without any order as to costs. 

19. In the light of the facts and circumstances discussed above, we find illegality and infirmity in the impugned judgment, which in our view calls for interference. 

20. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed without any order as to costs.

The judgment and order of the High Court Division is set-aside and thereby restored the judgment of the trial Court.

End.

full_judgment:
On an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure this Rule was issued at the instance of the petitioners calling upon the opposite party Nos.1-8 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 28-10-2015 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Bogra in Partition Appeal No.84 of 2006 disallowing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 22-6-2006 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Bogra in Partition Suit No. 58 of 1994 dismissing the suit should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the petitioner No.1, predecessor of petitioner Nos.2 and 3 named, Khaja Abdus Salek along with 6(six) others, as plaintiff, instituted Partition Suit No.58 of 1994 against the opposite parties, as defendant, for a decree of partition of the property mentioned in schedule to the plaint, stating that the suit property along with other non-suited property originally belonged to one Khaja Golam Mohiuddin who used to reside on the property by constructing dwelling house. He made an Waqf-fi-sabilillah for the non-suited property on 6-8-1923, wherein, he made a Wasiat to the effect that the suit property in question shall devolve upon Tarunnessa and youngest son Khaja Nazmul Huq on the east and elder son Khaja Kornoruddin on the west and also declared that his daughters will not be entitled to get any property in the homestead and its surrounding garden. Out of suit plot, Golam Mohiuddin made waqf for 0.03600 sataks in favour of Family Mosque. Khaja Golam Mohiuddin died leaving son Khaja Komoruddin and Khaja Nazmul Huq, 2(two) daughters Hamida Khatun and Ayesha Khatun. As per terms and conditions of waqf deed his wife Tarunnessa and 2(two) sons Khaja Komoruddin and Khaja Nazmul Huq by family settlement got the property and had been in possession of the same and the daughters also got other property. 

3. Khaja Komoruddin while in possession of his share erected a shop on a part of the suit plot with the knowledge of other heirs of Golam Mohiuddin and had been possessing the same for more than statutory period of limitation. Komoruddin died leaving 2(two) wives Tohurunnessa and Maher Afjan, 6(six) sons namely, Khaja Bosir Uddin, Khaja Saif Uddin, Khaja Tayebuddin, Khaja Hafezar and plaintiff Nos.1 and 2 and daughter Zohura Khatun, who inherited the property left by Komoruddin as per their share. During revisional survey, MRR Khatian recorded in the name of the plaintiffs but share has been wrongly recorded against their names. MRR Khatian is wrong, 0.8338 satakas ought to have been recorded in Plot No.1709 and 0.0475 in Plot No.1712. The suit property has not been partitioned among the co-sharers by metes and bound. When the plaintiffs demanded partition of the property, the defendants were killing time on various pleas and finally on 1-1-1994 they denied partition of the property hence, the present suit for partition. 

4. Defendant Nos.11-14, 24, 25, 33-39, 41, 42 and 43 filed 3(three) sets of written statements denying the material facts made in the plaint. Among the defendants only defendant Nos.33-39 and 41 contested the suit contending inter alia, that the property in question originally belonged to their predecessor Khaja Golam Mohiuddin. Plot No.1709 comprising homestead, graveyard and Mosque of the plaintiffs and defendants. On Plot No.1712 there is a shop house. A portion measuring 0.03600 sataks under Plot No.1709 is being used for Mosque and graveyard and on remaining land homestead of Khaja Golam Mohiuddin. Khaja Golam Mohiuddin made a waqf on 6-8-1923 for non-suited property and made Wasiat to the effect that remaining portion of Plot Nos.1709 and 1712 will be inherited by his wife Tarunnessa and youngest son Khaja Nazmul Huq on the east and eldest son Khaja Komoruddin on the west. Accordingly, after the death of Khaja Golam Mohiuddin they got their respective property and had been possessing the same as per Wasiat and by amicable partition among the heirs Khaja Komoruddin got entire quantum of land measuring 0.0475 sataks in Plot No.1712 and 1/2 of Plot No.1709. While he was in possession and enjoyment of the property died leaving 2(two) wives, 6(six) sons plaintiff Nos.1 and 2, Khaja Bosir Uddin, Khaja Mohiuddin, Khaja Tayebuddin and predecessor of the defendant Nos.33-39 and 41 named Hafezer Rahman and daughter Zohura Khatun. Among the heirs of Komoruddin, there has been a family partition and on the basis of amicable partition Khaja Hafezer Rahman obtained 0.0350 sataks of land from Plot No.1712 including his purchased land measuring 0.593/8 by kabala dated 14-5-1957. 

5. Said Hafezer Rahman had been possessing the property in Plot No.1712 with the knowledge of all exclusively and complelety ousting the plaintiffs and other defendants in suit for more than statutory period of limitation and used to run a hotel situated on the suit Plot No.1712. Hafezer Rahman died leaving defendant Nos.33-39 and 41 who inherited the same and have been possessing for more than statutory period of limitation by erecting pucca shop by demolishing mud house existing on the suit Plot No.1712. On the ground floor there is a hotel named "Ittehad Hotel and Restaurant" and 1st floor of the building let out for commercial purposes to different persons. Defendant No.33 has been running the Hotel and Restaurant on the Suit Plot No.1712 measuring 0.0350 sataks and the rest 0.0125 sataks fell in the share of Khaja Boshiruddin on the east who constructed a sami pucca tinshed house on the said property and had been in possession with the knowledge of the plaintiff and others. On the death of Khaja Boshiruddin his heirs have been owning and possessing the said quantum of land. In the manner aforesaid these defendants got 0.0350 sataks of land from Plot No.1712 and their respective share in Plot No.1709. The plaintiffs, have no title and possession in Plot No.1712 which fell in the share of Hafezer Rahman and Khaja Boshiruddin by amicable partition among the heirs of Komoruddin. The plaintiffs obtained their share from other plots but because of increase of price of the property the plaintiffs with mala fide intention and for illegal and undue gain instituted the present suit claiming partition of the property which was partitioned more than 60(sixty) years ago, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

6. The trial court framed 6(six) issues for determination of the dispute. Plaintiff No.1 himself deposed as PW 1, defendant No.33 himself deposed as DW 1 and one Ashraf Ali as DW 2. Both the parties submitted some documents in support of their respective claim which were duly marked as exhibits. The trial court considering evidences on record both oral and documentary dismissed the suit. 

7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the trial court, the plaintiffs preferred Partition Appeal No.84 of 2006 before the learned District Judge, Bogra. Eventually, the said appeal was heard and disposed of by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Bogra on transfer who upon hearing by the impugned judgment and decree dated 28-10-2015 disallowed the appeal 
affirming the judgment and decree of the trial court. At this juncture, the plaintiff No.3 and heirs of plaintiff No.2 moved this Court by filing this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule and order of status-quo. 

8. Mr Md Abdul Kader Newaz, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that there is no dispute that the suit property fell in the share of Khaja Komoruddin son of Khaja Golam Mohiuddin and it is also not disputed that there are Mosque and family graveyard on Plot No.1709 measuring 0.03600 sataks. It is also not disputed that on Plot No.1709 there is homestead of Khaja Golam Mohiuddin, predecessor of the parties to the suit. He further submits that dispute between the parties mainly arose regarding Plot No.1712 on which a hotel named Ittehad Hotel and Restaurant is standing and being run by defendant No.33 which is ejmali property and has not been partitioned among the co-sharers by metes and bound. 

9. In support of his such submissions he submits that in MRR Khatian name of the plaintiffs are appearing though the quantum of land has been shown wrongly. It is also argued that had there been any amicable partition among the co-sharer of Plot No.1712, MRR and present khatian ought to have been stood recorded in the name of Hafezer Rahman or his heirs but no such record of right could be submitted by the contesting defendants to show that their predecessor got the property by amicable partition among the heirs of Komoruddin. He submits that since the record of right clearly shows that the plaintiffs and defendants are co-sharers in the suit property and in the absence of any evidence both oral and documentary, the trial court as well as the appellate court ought to have decreed the suit for partition allotting saham to the plaintiffs as per their share but both the courts below instead of decreeing the suit most unfortunately made out a 3rd case of amicable partition among the co-sharers observing that the property under Plot No.1712 fell in the share of Hafizer Rahman measuring 0.0350 sataks and in the share of Khaja Boshiruddin measuring 0.0125 sataks without any evidence. 

10. He candidly submits that their has been some lacuna in drafting plaint and also conducting the case before the trial court as well as before the appellate court but for the fault of the lawyer unless an opportunity is given to the petitioners to get their plaint suitably amended and adduce sufficient evidences before the court by sending back the suit on remand to the trial court, the petitioners shall be highly prejudiced and non-suited, as such, the suit may kindly be sent back on remand considering that this is a suit for partition. 

11. Mr Md Nurul Amin, learned Senior Advocate with Mr Ashraful Alam appearing for the opposite party Nos.1-8 at the very outset submits that as per record of right Plot No.1709 contain 2.0275 sataks, the plaintiffs, in the schedule to the plaint mentioned the quantum of land as 1.4675 sataks. Subsequently, at the appellate stage by amendment of plaint totally deleted Plot No.1709 from the plaint by order dated 30-4-2008 making the plaint to suffer from defect of hotchpotch. He further submits that unless all the property left by Komoruddin are included in the plaint, only in respect of one plot their cannot be any partition among the co-sharers. He further submits that the plaintiffs rightly included 2(two) plots in the plaint though quantum of property shown wrongly in Plot No.1709 before the trial court but on appeal by way of amendment the plaintiffs deleted Plot No.1709 as a whole only seeking partition in respect of Plot No.1712 on which admittedly the defendant Nos.33-39 and 41's predecessor was in possession and one Khaja Boshiruddin possessing a portion of the land on the east. As such, both the courts below while dismissing the suit and disallowing the appeal concurrently found that the plaintiff No.1 while deposing before the court unequivocally admitted that the plaintiffs are not in possession in Plot No.1712 from the time of predecessor of the defendant Nos.33-39 and 41 and also admitted that the plaintiffs have been possessing their share by amicable arrangement among the co-sharers, the heirs of Komoruddin. He further submits that though in MRR khatian some plaintiffs' name are appearing but facts remain, the plaintiffs could not substantiate their claim that they as co-sharer ever possessed the suit property under Plot No.1712, moreover, admitted that in the year 1964 when the contesting defendant No.33 obtained sanction for construction of pucca shop house on Plot No.1712 from local Purashava he filed an objection which was rejected establishing that the contesting defendants are in possession of the property from the time of their predecessor Hafezer Rahman who purchased a portion of the land in the year 1957. As such, both the courts below rightly dismissed the suit holding that the plaintiffs could not prove their case and at the appellate stage gave up their claim in Plot No.1709 for partition and also admitted that the property under Plot No.1712 measuring 0.0475 sataks out of which 0-0350 sataks are in possession of the contesting defendants for more than statutory period of limitation. 

12. Heard the learned Advocates of both the parties, have gone through the revisional application, plaint in suit, written statement, evidences both oral and documentary and the impugned judgment and decree of both the courts below. 

13. The trial court while dismissing the suit observed that Khaja Abdus Salek as PW 1 deposed for and on behalf of all the plaintiffs in suit in support of their claim and in cross he clearly stated that.;
“খাজা কমর উদ্দিনের ত্যাক্ত সম্পত্তি আমরা তার ওয়ারিশণণ মৌখিক বাটায়ারা মূলে দখল করছি। মৌখিক বাটোয়ারা ১৯৬৫ সালে হয় । তখন খাজা হাকিজার জীবিত ছিলেন । তিনি আরও বলেন যে, আমি তহশিলদার ছিলাম । আমাদের জমি জায়গা কাগজ পত্র হিসাব নিকাশ বিবয়ে আমার ধারণা ছিল । ইত্তেহাদ হোটেলটি ১৯৪৬ সালে নির্মাণ হয়। তখন থেকে আজ অবধি ২/৪ বার হোটেলটি ভাঙ্গা গড়া মেরামত হয়। এটি প্রথমে কীচা ঘর নির্মাণ হয় । বর্তমানে ইটের গীথুনী ছাদযুক্ত দোতলা । এই হোটেল বা দোকারঘর বিষয়ে আমার নামে কোন কাগজ নাই । আমার ভাই হাফিজের নামে থাকতে পারে । তাদের ছেলেদের নামে বর্তমানে কাগজ পত্র আছে কিনা বলতে পারি না।”

14. He further stated that after the death of Khaja Hafezer the defendant No.33 running the hotel business "Ittehad Hotel and Restaurant" on the ground floor and let out first floor to different tenants and collecting rents by him. It is also admitted that he has no paper and documents in his name to show that the plaintiffs ever possessed the property under Plot No.1712 and also admitted that the hotel shop constructed by the contesting defendants and all the papers and documents are in their names. And finally the trial court came into conclusion that the property among the co-sharers had already been partitioned amicably and said amicable partition become acted upon by act and conduct of the heirs of Komoruddin and also by supporting documents. Before the appellate court the plaintiffs got their plaint amended and left out Plot No.1709 as a whole from their claim leaving only Plot No.1712. The appellate court while disallowing the appeal observed that CS Plot No.1709 contain 2.027 acres and Plot No.1712 contain 0.0475 acres and the plaintiffs as heirs of Komoruddin can claim partition as per their shares in both the plots but the plaintiffs all of a sudden deleted major portion of the property from the plaint making the suit defect of hotchpotch. Unless all the property left by Komoruddin is included in the hotchpotch, share cannot be distributed among the co-sharers allotting saham and effecting delivery of possession maintaining their possession in the property. As such, without bringing all the properties into hotchpotch a suit for partition is not at all maintainable. Though the appeal was preferred by all the plaintiffs in suit and their successors but among the plaintiffs only plaintiff No.3 and the heirs of plaintiff No.2 preferred this revision and other plaintiffs did not rush to the court against the judgment and decree of the appellate court meaning thereby that they abandoned or gave up their claim in the property sought to be partitioned. 

15. In this peculiar situation the statements made in the plaint and on that basis the present petitioners cannot get any relief as their share in the property has not been clearly quantified and specified. 

16. From the evidences available in record and admitted by the PW 1 this Court also found that the property under Plot No.1712 are in the possession of defendant No.33-39 and 41 and the portion on the east measuring 00125 sataks in the possession of Khaja Boshiruddin and on his death now under possession of his heirs and admittedly they have been possessing the property from the time of their predecessor more than statutory period of limitation by ousting the plaintiffs, as such, the claim of amicable partition among the heirs of Komoruddin has been established by evidences, in particular, admitted by PW 1. Since an objection was filed against sanction of defendant No.33 by the plaintiff before the municipal authority in the year 1964 and rejected, it is established that the predecessor of the contesting defendant Hafezer Rahman was in exclusive possession of the property in Plot No.1712 by amicable arrangement among the co-sharers ousting the plaintiffs and their predecessor. 

17. However, a suit for partition is maintainable by any co-sharer by bringing all the property into hotchpotch and giving a clear picture as to acquisition of their shares in the property but in the instant case though at the first instance included 2(two) plots of land mentioning their claim but for the reason of subsequent amendment deleting major portion of the property from the plaint and also not preferring revision by major portion of the plaintiffs in suit giving up their claim in the property, the statements made in the plaint and claim of the present 3(three) petitioners has become absolutely vague and uncertain. Consequently, their claim must fail on the ground of defect of hotchpotch and vagueness of their claim in respect of their share in the property and clear and definite statement regarding their possession. 

18. In view of the above, this Court finds that both the courts below in dismissing the suit as well as disallowing the appeal have not committed any illegality in law and any error in the decisions occasioning failure of justice. 

19. Before parting with the case, I like to say a few words to the effect that before the trial court as well as the appellate court concerned conducting lawyer for the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner recklessly handled the case and took step highly detrimental to the interest of the plaintiffs leaving no way to get relief in the suit as well as get the suit back on remand to the trial court. 

20. Taking into considering the above, I find no merit in the Rule. 

21. In the result, the Rule is discharged, however, without any order as to costs. 

22. Order of status-quo granted at the time of issuance of the Rule is stand vacated. 
Communicate a copy of the judgment to the Court concerned and send down the lower court records at once. 

End.
