full_judgment:
In the instant review application filed under Order 47 Rule 1 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why delay of 3,572 days in filing the review application should not be condoned and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. In the application for condonation of delay it is stated that the present petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.28 of 1998 before the then subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka for a declaration that the osiatnama described in the schedule is forged and illegal and further declaration that the plaintiffs are absolute owners of their inherited share of the schedule properties as well as partition of the suit land. 

3. The present opposite parties as defendants contested the suit by filing written statement which on hearing was decreed vide judgment and decree dated 4-5-2002 whereas the appellate Court in Title Appeal No.284 of 2002 remanded the said suit to the Trial Court vide judgment and decree dated 28-2-2004 and the Trial Court after hearing dismissed the suit vide judgment and decree dated 28-8-2007 whereupon the plaintiffs filed Title Appeal No.406 of 2007 before the District Judge, Dhaka and on hearing the appellate Court dismissed the appeal vide judgment and decree dated 9-9-2008 whereupon the present petitioners preferred Civil Revision No.4103 of 2008 before the High Court division and during pendency of the Rule a joint compromise petition has been filed by both the parties on 26-10-2011 and accordingly the Rule was disposed of on 27-10-2011 as per the terms of the compromise. 

4. It is stated that as per terms No. 6(ছ) and 6(জ), the petitioners got certain quantum of land but it appears that earlier the opposite parties by concealing the facts transferred the said land vide Annexure-A, Al -A5. It is averred that after effecting compromise, the petitioners did not go to Village home to take possession of the disputed land reposing trust upon the opposite parties and both the parties engaged themselves in developing the properties situated at Dhaka, but recently when the petitioners took initiative to take possession of the land, they came to know that the lands were sold by the opposite parties before entering into compromise and then the petitioners on causing search to the sub-registry office obtained certified copies of those transfer deed and became certain about the transfer as aforementioned whereby it is clearly apparent that the opposite parties by committing fraud entered into compromise and got the case disposed of by concealing facts. It is further stated that when the matter came to the fore, Covid-l9 ingulfed the country and it was not possible for the tadbirkar to meet the engaged lawyer for taking necessary steps and subsequently the petitioner's tadbirkar himself inflected with Covid-19 virus and after getting recovery by suffering about two months he met with the engaged lawyer on 25-10-2001 who advised to procure necessary papers for filing review and he handed over necessary papers to him and accordingly the instant review application has been filed causing delay of 3572 days which should be condoned. 

5. The opposite party No.1-5 filed a counter affidavit denying the claim of the petitioner and contended that the grounds for condonation of delay is not correct as the applicants used to live in village home and sold 2.60 acres of land to Abdul Mannan on 18-1-2003 and 1.50 acres of land to Mostofa Miah who in turn sold the same to Abdul Mannan by deed of sale dated 17-1-2004 and thereby the applicants sold 4.10 acres of land which they got vide Paragraph 6(ছ) and 6 (জ) of the compromise petition. It is averred that opposite parties sold their portion of land as mentioned in paragraph 6(ছ) and 6 (জ) of compromise petition. It is also stated that the petitioner's purported knowledge dated 27-10-2011 is not at all correct as they had been continuously living in the village home. It is averred that the delay in filing the review application on the ground of Covid-19 pandemic is also not factually correct as excepting 4 months the Court was opened all through. It is averred that upon filing joint application by both the parties civil revision No. 4103 of 2008 was disposed of and as per paragraph 6(ক) 99 ajutangsha land out of 4.95 decimal was allotted to applicants and remaining 3.96 decimal land was allotted to the opposite parties. It is further stated that as per condition of compromise, the applicants and opposite parties executed unregistered property development agreement with M/s Modern Builders on 6-11-2011 and subsequently deed of irrevocable power of attorney was executed on 29-11-2016 with Advance Consultant Ltd. to build 9 storeyed building as per the compromise petition. It is further stated that the developer company was supposed to complete construction work and to handover flats to the land owner viz the applicants and opposite parties within 40 months but they failed to do so whereupon the opposite parties took the matter for arbitration but the present petitioners at the instigation of the developer company initiated the instant review petition with a view to jeopardize the development work. It is also averred that as per condition No.3 of compromise deed, the applicants admitted that they have no claim regarding the property sold by the opposite parties from paragraph 6(ছ) and 6 (জ) and 6(ঝ) of the compromise petition and also resolved that if there be any legal complexity regarding the transferred land, it will be resolved accordingly. It is further averred that the other lands situated at Dokhin Char Elahi having area of 10. 45 acres have been occupied by the petitioners though the petitioners and opposite parties jointly owned the said properties. 

6. By filing an affidavit-in-reply the petitioners asserted that the petitioner inherited half of the land in Diara plot No.3145 and 3146 and portion of which they sold to Abdul Mannan and Mostofa Mia. It is asserted that the petitioners never entered into collusion with developer company and with bonafide intention filed the review petition. It is asserted that the deed of compromise dated 6-11-2011 is created and forged one. It is further asserted that the transfer of portion of the land prior of compromise has been admitted by the opposite parties in the counter affidavit and, as such, clear fraud has been proved. By filing another affidavit in reply the petitioners submitted copies of the deeds in question whereby the opposite parties have purportedly transferred land vide Annexure E, E-1 and E-2. 

7. Mr Naim Ahmed, learned advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the opposite parties committed fraud regarding the terms and condition of the compromise petition allotting the property of 6 (জ) and 6(ঝ) in favour of the petitioners while they earlier transferred the said land to others and fraud vitiated everything and, as such, the judgment and decree passed on compromise is required to be set-aside on review but as there occurred delay 3,572 days in filing the review application the said delay should be condoned. Dr. Naim next submits that the grounds for causing delay in filing the review application has been clearly and conspicuously narrated in the application for condonation of delay and, as such, the delay as mentioned should be condoned for proper adjudication of the disputes. Learned advocate next submits that the petitioners were not aware about the earlier sale by the opposite parties as the petitioners did not go to village home for quite long period and when they came to know about the transfer, they decided to file review application for setting aside the compromise decree but due to Covid pandemic which engulfed the entire country, they could not file the review application within the time and, as such, the unintentional delay should be condoned. 

8. On the other hand Mr Muhammad Shafique Ullah, learned advocate appearing for the opposite parties submits that the petitioners reside in village home and they are aware about the transfer of property in question much earlier and, as such, the instant application filed with inordinate delay should not be condoned as the opposite parties have acquired vested right by long lapse of time. Mr Muhammad Shafique Ullah learned advocate next submits that the applicants having resident of village home sold 2.60 acres of land to Abdul Mannnan on 18-1-2003 and 1.50 acres of land to Mostofa Miah who in turn sold the same to Abdul Mannan by deed of sale dated 17-1-2004 and thereby they sold 4.10 acres of land which they got vide paragraph 6(জ) and 6(ঝ) of the compromise petition and, as such, the instant review application filed with long delay cannot be sustained. Learned advocate further submits that the date of purported knowledge as mentioned in the application for condonation of delay on 27-10-2011 is not at all correct which has been made with a view to rescue themselves from long delay in filing the review application and, as such, the delay should not be condoned. Learned advocate further submits that the petitioners at the instance of developer company have filed the instant review application which defaulted in completing the project as per the agreement entered into by the opposite parties and petitioners and, as such, there is no bonafide in the present application for condonation of delay. Learned advocate also submits that the petitioners have executed an unregistered deed admitting the contents of solenama and also executed and registered a nadabipatra which signifies that the solanama in question is genuine, bonafide and reliable but the petitioners filed the instant application at the behest of the developer company and, as such, the long delay having occurred should not be condoned. Learned advocate averred that the opposite party have initiated arbitration proceeding for the breach committed by the developer company but with a view to forestall the arbitration proceeding, the petitioners have filed the instant review application which is liable to be rejected on the score of long delay. 

9. Admittedly earlier litigation between the parties was apparently resolved in civil Revision No. 4103 of 2008 as per the terms of written compromise whereby the present petitioners got the land as mentioned in paragraph 6(ছ) and 6 (জ) of compromise petition dated 27-10-2011 but the specific contention of the petitioners are that earlier the opposite parties transferred the said land vide Annexure-A, A l -A5 and it is averred that the petitioners got no prior knowledge regarding the said transfer as they did not go to village home to take possession of the disputed land and it is further averred that they came to know about such transfer recently when they took initiative to take possession of the land and according to the petitioners, the opposite parties have committed fraud upon the petitioners in disposing the earlier suit by compromise. 

10. On perusal of Annexure-A, Al -A5 it appears that those deeds have apparently been executed by the opposite parties prior to compromise entered into between the parties. It is common knowledge that fraud vitiates everything and whether fraud has been committed or not is to be ascertained in the review petition having filed by the present petitioners. The petitioners also stated that clue to Covid-19 virus, functioning of the Court was stalled for quite number of months and it took huge time to resume normal functioning of the court which is also a ground formulated by the petitioners. So apparently the petitioners have been able to give cogent explanation in causing delay of filing the instant review application. 

11. In the case of Nasimuddin Mia vs Monindra Kumar Maloo and others 2 BLC 83 it is held that, as the allegation of fraud and the violation of terms of original agreement has been proved in the matter of exchange of the property between the parties, the suit is not barred by limitation as it will start from the date of knowledge of fraud practiced. 

12. In the case of Emarat Ali vs State 57 DLR 620 it is held that: 
"where the Court before exercising the power under section 5 of the Limitation Act feels satisfied upon the facts of the case under consideration that the explanation given for the delay is sufficient, the discretion under section 5 of the Limitation Act should be exercised and the Court should take a liberal view in considering the case shown by the applicant. The Court should not press for explanation of each hours or each days delay. Considering the peculiar circumstances of this case, it would be sufficient if each days delay is not established conclusively but may satisfy the Court by furnishing some general reasonable explanation. Under section 5 of the limitation Act, the petitioner is entitled to condonation of delay if he can satisfy the court that he had sufficient cause for not making the application within the period fixed by statute. Whether or not there was sufficient cause for not coming to court within the period prescribed by Limitation act is a question of fact which is to be determined keeping in view all the attending circumstances. The words 'sufficient cause' should receive a liberal construction so as to advance substantial justice when negligence, nor inaction, nor want of bonafide is imputable to the applicant. Appellant is only required to satisfy the Court that he was unable to prefer appeal in time on account of some misadventure on which it ought to have been presented beyond prescribed period and it is not necessary for him to account for inactivity during the entire period prescribed by law." 

13. It is also held therein that: 
"A genuine or good cause or a cause which is beyond the control of a party or a cause which is unavoidable despite care and attention may constitute sufficient cause. Sufficient cause means something beyond the control of the party. That constitutes sufficient cause cannot be laid down by hard and fast rules. Broadly speaking, however, it connotes something beyond the control of the party. It must be determined by a reference to the circumstances of each particular case."  

14. In the case of Golam Hossain vs Ahdus Sukur Bhuiyan and others 13 BLC 817 it is held by a bench of this Court that: 
"Delving into facts and circumstances of the case as emerged from statements made in potions and documents annexed as Annexures and taking into account object of doing substantial justice to parties concerned, I am of this considered view that section 14 of The limitation Act can be very much pressed into service in support of case of pre-emptee-petitioner and pre-emptee-petitioner has made out a case which persuaded me to condone the delay, though inordinate, but without any fault of pre-emptee-petitioner. Discharging Rules on technical ground of limitation would not in any way advance the interest of justice. Fate of pre-emption Miscellaneous Case can be very much determined in Civil Revision petitions. It is posited here that technicality of law of limitation cannot prevent this Court from doing substantial justice when pre-emptee-petitioner could make out a case for condonation of delay and, also, in getting Civil Revision petitions heard and disposed of on merit. It is posited here that Primary function of a court is to adjudicate dispute between the parties advance substantial justice time limit fix for approaching the Court in different situation is not because on the expiry of such time a bad case would transfer into a good cause. If the explanation offered for condonation of delay does not smack of malafide the Court must show utmost consideration to the suitor. In Nand Klishor vs state of Punjab Supreme Court of India under peculiar circumstances of the case condoned that delay in approaching the Court after about 31 years. In N Balakrishna vs M. Krishna Murthy Supreme Court of India held: The purpose of Limitation Act was not to destroy the rights. It is founded on public policy fixing a life span for the legal remedy for general welfare." 

15. So in the above facts and circumstances and on consideration of the aforesaid ratios the Rule has got merit and the delay of 3572 days requires to be condoned. 

16. Consequently the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost. 

The review application will appear in the list on 31-5-22 for hearing as in-re matter. 

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 26-11-2006 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2360 of 1997)
full_judgment:
Md Nuruzzaman, J: This Civil Appeal, by leave, has arisen out of the judgment and order dated 26-11-2006 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2360 of 1997 making the Rule absolute thereby setting aside the judgment and decree dated 27-4-1997 passed by the Additional District Judge, First Court, Sylhet in Title Appeal No.251 of 1985 and reversing the judgment and decree dated 27-6-1984 decreeing the suit in part passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Additional Court, Sylhet in Title Suit No.33 of 1979.
2. Facts leading, to filing of this civil appeal, in short, are that one Md Ahalullah, the predecessor of the petitioners as the plaintiff filed Title Suit No.152 of 1975 before the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 2nd Court, Sylhet which was transferred to the Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 1st Additional Court, Sylhet and renumbered as Title Suit No.33 of 1979 for specific performance of contract against the present respondent Nos.4-5 including their mother Renu Bala Das impleading them as defendant Nos.1-3 and including present respondent No.6 as proforma defendant No.4 stating, inter alia, that Kailash Chandra Das, predecessor of the present-respondent Nos.4-5 being the owners and possessors of the suit land, proposed to sell the suit land to the plaintiff for Taka 25,000 and the plaintiff agreed to purchase the same. Thereafter, the aforesaid Kailash Chandra Das executed and registered a Bainapatra dated 27 Sraban, 1379 BS corresponding to .12-8-1972 in favour of the plaintiff on receipt of Taka 2,000 from the plaintiff. Said Kailash Chandra Das executed and registered another Bainapatra on 7-41973 corresponding to 24 Chaitra 1379 in favour of the plaintiff on receiving of Taka 1,000. Thereafter, on the several occasions by installment said Kailash Chandra Das and his son defendant No.2 in total received Taka 10,380 from the plaintiff and his son. Thereafter, the plaintiff came to know that the defendants are trying to sell the suit land to others. The plaintiff asked the defendant Nos.1-3 to execute and register the conveyance in favour of him on acceptance of balance amount from the plaintiff but the defendants refused to do so. Hence, the plaintiff was compelled to institute the suit to get a conveyance executed and registered by the defendant Nos.1-3 in respect of the suit land. During pendency of the suit the plaintiff by way of amendment of the plaint alternative relief was sought that if, the plaintiff could not prove any claim of the suit plots for specific performance of contract, in that case, he will be entitled to get back principal amount with compensation for the amount, he has already paid for the said plot. Thereafter, the plaintiff by filing an application sought to omit the above alternative relief which was allowed by the trial Court but the said order of omitting the alternative prayer was not challenged by the contesting defendants.
3. The defendant Nos.1-2 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter-alia, that the suit land was originally belonged to Kailash Chandra Das and after the death of the aforesaid Kailash Chandra Das his interest in respect of the suit land developed upon the defendant Nos.l-3 as his legal heirs. The defendant Nos.1-3 sold the Suit Plot Nos.1, 2 and 3 of the plaint schedule to Assoddar Ali by a registered sale deed dated 20-10-1974 for maintenance, educational expenses of the defendant Nos.2 and 3 and for meeting up the expenses of Sraddah of Kailash Chandra Das. The defendant Nos.1-3 sold the land of Plot No.6 of the plaint schedule to Ahmed Ali and Abdul Ali at a consideration of Taka 8,000 by a sale deed dated 15-1-1975 and gave possession of the same in their favour. The defendant Nos.1-3 kept the land of Plot Nos.4 and 5 of the plaint schedule under the care of Ahmed Ali and Abdul Ali. The predecessor of the defendants Kailash Chandra Das did not execute any bainapatra in favour of the plaintiff. The alleged bainapatra are forged, collusive, paper transaction without any consideration and that the defendants never received any amount of money from the plaintiff and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed.
4. On conclusion of the trial, the learned Sub-Judge (now Joint District Judge), 1st Additional Court, Sylhet considering the evidences and documents on record decreed the suit in part by his judgment and decree dated 27-6-1984.
5. Feeling aggrieved, by the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiff as appellant preferred Title Appeal No.251 of 1985 before the learned District Judge, Sylhet. Eventually, on transfer, the said appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Sylhet who by his judgment and decree dated 27-4-1997 allowed the appeal and thereby set-aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court and decreed the suit.
6. Feeling aggrieved, by the judgment and decree dated 27-4-1997 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Sylhet, the added defendant Nos.5-7 preferred Civil Revision No.2360 of 1997 before the High Court Division and obtained the Rule.
7. In due course, a Single Bench of the High court Division upon hearing the parties made the Rule absolute by the impugned judgment and order dated 26-11-2006 and thereby set-aside the judgment and decree dated 27-4-199; passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Sylhet in Title Appeal No.251 of 1985 and thereby affirmed the judgment and decree dated 27-6-1984 passed by the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge, 1st Additional Court, Sylhet in Title Suit No.33 of 1979.
8. The plaintiff as petitioners herein feeling aggrieved by the impugned judgment and order dated 26-11-2006 of the High Court Division preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.473 of 2007 before this Division and obtained leave, which, gave rise to the instant appeal.
9. Mr Khair Ezaz Maswood, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellants has submitted that the suit schedules contain several plots and khatians and the plaintiff amended the plaint to the effect that the refund of baina money may be allowed if the claim of any of the plot is not proved, but in this case, the plaintiff successfully proved the claim in each and every plot of the suit schedule of the bainapatra by examining the oral and documentary evidences and that the PWs' corroborated each other and that the defendants' side could not extract any contradiction upon cross-examination of the PW's. The DW's as well could not prove the defence case. Moreover, the plaintiff amended the plaint deleting the alternative prayer which was allowed vide order No.91 dated 19-6-1984 but the High Court Division without appreciating the consequence of the withdrawal of the alternative prayer vide order No.91 dated 19-6-1984 passed the impugned judgment and order on the erroneous findings that the plaintiff amended the plaint claiming alternative relief for which he is not entitled to decree of specific performance of contract which is nothing, rather, emerged on the basis of misconceived appreciation about law and facts and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division cannot be sustained in law. He has further submitted that as per settled principle of law when the plaintiff's first prayer is for a decree for specific performance of contract and alternatively he prays for refund of the earnest money in the event of refusal of specific performance of contract it cannot be argued that in the facts of an alternative prayer for the refund of the earnest money the plaintiff is not entitled to a decree for specific performance of contract. The High Court Division erred in law and passed the impugned judgment and order against the settled principle of law only considering the alternative prayer of the plaintiff. Moreover, said alternative prayer was amended and thrown-up by the plaintiff on 19-6-1984 vide, order No.91 which was unchallenged, as not challenged by the defendants in the higher Court, thus, such give-up it is meaning that they have conceded order of withdrawal of the alternative prayer and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be interfered with by this Division. He has finally submitted that the specific case of the defendant Nos.1-3 that the bainapatra was collusive, fraudulent and forged and that there was no case of the defendants that the plaintiff had alternative prayer for refund of bainapatra money with compensation but the High Court Division made the Rule absolute considering the alternative prayer of the plaintiff without rebutting the findings of facts as discussed and found correct by the last Court of facts as Appellate Court and decreed the suit allowing the appeal instead of decree in part passed by the trial Court and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be set-aside. Hence, the instant appeal may kindly be allowed.
10. Per contra, Mr AM Amin Uddin, the learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the respondents has submitted in supports of the impugned judgment of the High Court Division. He has further submitted that the plaintiff filed an application with alternative prayer dated 20-12-1977 for amendment of the plaint for an alternative relief for return of the consideration amount together compensation at the rate of Taka 25% in the event of his failure to get a decree for specific performance of contract, the trial Court decreed the suit on solatium under section 22 of the Specific Relief Act. No error of law or facts has been occurred in granting such decree. He has further submitted that the lower appellate Court wrongly and illegally decreed the suit for execution of sale deed by the defendant Nos.1- 3, the heirs of the original owner of Kailash Chandra Das. The sale deed executed by the defendant Nos.1-3 in favour of defendant Nos.5-7 remains untouched, unaffected. He has also submitted that the defendant Nos.5-7 are transferee for value against consideration in good faith without notice of earlier agreement for sale by Kailash Chandra Das predecessor in interest of the vendor. They are in possession of the suit properties by dint of valid registered documents. The learned Senior counsel finally referring section 27(b) of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 has argued that the suit against the added defendant Nos.5-7 herein respondent Nos.1(a) to 1(i), 2 and 3 is hits by the provisions of that section. Therefore, the petitioners cannot get any relief against them. Hence, the High Court Division rightly made the Rule absolute. Therefore, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.
11. We have heard Mr Khair Ezaz Maswood and Mr AM Amin Uddin, the learned Senior Counsels for the respective parties. Perused the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and other connected materials on record.
12. The crux point as per leave granting order whether the High Court Division is right in making the Rule absolute and setting aside the judgment of the Appellate Court below without rebutting concurrent findings of facts and without appreciating the consequence of withdrawing of alternative prayer.
13. At this turning point, let us anatomize whether the submissions of the learned counsel for appellant or respondents are equitable.
14. We have carefully scrutinized the testimonies of all PWs and DWs. On scrutiny of the testimonies of the PWs it is well founded that they have proved the case of the plaintiff's side by giving evidences in vividly supporting each other's testimonies. However, in cross-examination, the defence could not make out material contradiction regarding material points that is the date of time and payment of the consideration as stated in Bainapathra exhibits. Moreover, PW 1-the hand writing expert in his report has vividly given opinion that the signature of the Kailash Chandra Das, the predecessors of the defendant Nos.1-3 given in the Bainapatra exhibits is genuine. In this turning point, both the Courts below found that the opinion of the hand writing expert is genuine and correct. Both the Courts below are also on the opinion that contract is genuine. However, the trial Court opined that except payment of Taka 3,000 (three thousand) rest of the payments were not proved. Therefore, the trial Court decreed the suit in part and Court of appeal below decreed the suit setting aside the decree of the trial Court with a direction to the plaintiff appellant to pay rest of the amount of Bainanama, i.e. Taka 23,000 (Taka twenty three thousand).
15. On examination of the order No.91 dated 19-6-1984 passed by the trial court it is found that the said alternative prayer was withdrawn by the plaintiff by amending the plaint. As per accepted principle of amendment of pleadings, once an amendment of the pleadings is allowed the amendment will relate back to the date of the institution of the suit. As to when an amendment of the plaint may be allowed by the Court one of the earliest pronouncements was made in the case of Kasisath Das vs Sadasiv Patnaik, (1893) ILR 20 Cal. 805 which is as follows:
"an amendment, so long as it does not alter the character of the suit, may be allowed at any time before judgment. The restriction is only as to the nature of the suit; the law prohibits any such amend-ment as would change the fundamental character of the suit; for example, a plaint cannot' be so amended as to convert a claim based on concoct into an action on tort. But an alteration in the relief does not alter the character of a suit."
16. The same view was maintained by the High Court Division in (Mrs) Nurun Nahar vs Mohd. Fazlur Rahman, reported in 1979 BSCR 135 = 27 DLR (AD) 103 and reiterated by this Division in Radha Krishna Jogani (Agarwalla) vs Dwarka Das Agarwalla and others reported in 1985 BLD (AD) 85 = 36 DLR (AD) 253.

17. In the case of Amena Khatun and others vs Hajee, Abdul Jabbar being dead his heirs: Mst. Maleka Banu and others reported in 1994 BLD (AD) 267 Appellate Division affirmed as follows:
"From the prayer in the plaint it appears that the plaintiff at prayer "Ka" prayed for specific p"rformance of contract in respect of the suit house of the defendant in pursuance of the agreement for sale dated 24-3-73. At prayer "Ga" the plaintiff prayed for refund of earnest money if the decree of specific performance of contract is refused by the Court. So, essentially the first prayer is for specific performance of contract and the prayer at "Ga" as mentioned above is an alternative prayer. Such prayer is ordinarily made, as in the event of refusal of specific performance of contract the plaintiff can get refund of the earnest money. Even without this prayer if a suit for specific performance of contract is dismissed, then the plaintiff is entitled to refund of the earnest money. So from this alternative prayer it cannot be argued that there being an alternative prayer for refund of the earnest money the plaintiff is not entitled to a decree for specific performance of contract."
18. Hence, our considered view is that High Court Division made overbearing error of laws setting aside the judgment and order of the appellate Court without appreciating the order No.91 dated 19-6-1989 of the trial Court and on that basis came to an erroneous finding that the plaintiff amended the plaint claiming alternative relief is in existence.
19. On perusal of the judgment of the trial Court it appears that the trial Court opined that "according to law bainapatra exhibits 3 and 3(a) did not create any title of the plaintiff in respect of the suit land. In view of the above discussion and on consideration of oral and documentary evidence on record the Court finds that the defendant Nos.5-7 purchased the lands out of the suit land from the defendant Nos.1-3 by the registered sale deed Exhibit A, A(1) and A(3). Those are for valuable consideration in good faith and without notice of the original contract held in between the plaintiff and Kailash Chandra Das and, as such, specific perfor-mance of contract held in between the plaintiff and Kailash Chandra Das cannot be enforced against the transferees defendant Nos.5-7".
20. However, it transpire that the PW 8 Tobarak Ali in his testimony stated that—
“বিবাদী মাহমুদ আলীর জমির লাগা আমার জমি আছে । জমিতে আমি চাষ করেছিলাম এবং মাহমুদ তার ভাই আব্দুল আলীসহ জমিতে তাদের জমি চাষ করেছিল এমন সময় বিবাদী আছালুল্লার কাছে জমি জমা সম্বন্ধে কথাবার্তা বলছিল । আমি সেখানে গিয়ে কি কথা হচ্ছে করে বলে আমরা এই জমি এতদিন ভাগী করছিলাম । এখন এ বাড়ী লোকখরিদ করার চুক্তি করেছে।”
21. So, the trial Court failed to appreciate the evidence of PW 8 in its true perspective. Moreso, the trial Court further opined that it is incumbent upon the plaintiff to prove that the defendant Nos.5, 6 and 7 were aware of the alleged contract made between the plaintiff and Kailash Chandra Das on the basis of baina-patras Exhibits 3 and 3(a) but he has failed to prove it by any reliable oral and documentary evidences. Such opinion of the trial Court is not only erroneous, rather, goes to the out of settle maxim of law. Because, the defendant Nos.5-7 claimed that they were not aware of the alleged contract made between the plaintiff and Kailash Chandra Das. So, according to provisions of section 103 of the Evidence Act, the burden of proof lies upon the added defendants to prove that they were not aware about the Exhibits 3 and 3A. The trial Court upon misreading of the evidence and provisions of law opined that the burden of proof lies upon the plaintiff.
22. For convenient of discussion let us study the provisions of section 103 of the Evidence Act, 1872 which runs as follows:
103. Burden of proof as to particular fact—The burden of proof as to any particular fact lies on that person who wishes the Court to believe in its existence, unless it is provided by any law that the proof of that fact shall lie on any particular person.
Illustrations:
(a) A prosecutes B for theft, and wishes the Court to believe that B admitted the theft to CA must prove the admission.
B wishes the Court to believe that, at the time in question, he was elsewhere. He must prove it.
23. It is our considered view that according to provisions of section 103 since the defendants came up with specific case that they were not aware about the exhibits-3 and 3A that are the bainapatras with Kailash Chandra Das and the predecessor of the plaintiff petitioner. Therefore, the burden of proof shifts upon the defendants to prove their part of the said specific case. But the defendant Nos.5-7 having miserably failed to discharge their onus to prove their part of the case. The trial Court committed serious error of law in decreeing the suit in-part. However, the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division also has committed same serious error of law in failing to appreciate the aforementioned provisions of section 103 of the Evidence Act in its true perspective.
24. In view of our above opinion, we can rely upon the case of Bulbul Begum vs Md Sanwar Belal and others reported in 8 BLC (AD) 97 wherein it was held by this Division that—
"Plaintiff discharged his burden of establishing the fact that defendant sent the rent for the month of May, 1988 after June 15, 1988. It was requirement for the defendant to disprove the said fact, but he did not take any step to disprove the oral as well as documentary evidence produced from the side of the plaintiff in assertion of the fact that rent for the month of May, 1988 was sent by money order after June 15, 1988".
25. In the case of Daliluddin Sheikh and others vs Alek Sheikh alias Abdul Malek Sheikh reported in 14 BLC (AD) 32 was held by this Division that—
"The High Court Division as well as the Court of appeal below were in error in holding that the defendants were to prove their case of auction purchase of the land of `Kha' and 'Ga' schedule and thus was in error in placing the onus on the defendants instead of the plaintiffs. The contention so made is of no substance since the defendants have claimed the land of the said two schedules, i.e. 'Kha' and 'Ga' schedules on the basis of alleged auction purchase, it was their obligation under the law to establish that they purchased the land in auction upon due compliance of the provisions of law".
26. Another pertinent question of law was raised by the learned Senior Counsel for the added respondents regarding the provisions of section 27(b) of the Specific Relief Act, 1877. Let us study the aforementioned provisions of law which runs as follows: —
"27. Except as otherwise provided by this Chapter, specific performance of a contract may be enforced against-
a) either party thereto;
b) any other person claiming under him by a title arising subsequently to the contract, except a transferee for value who has paid his money in good faith and without notice of the original' contract;
c) any person claiming under a title which, though prior to the contract and known to the plaintiff, might have been displaced by the defendant;
d) when a public company has entered into a contract and subsequently becomes amalgamated with another public company, the new company which arises out of the amalagation'
e) when the promoters of a public company have, before its incorporation, entered into a contract, the company: provided that the company has ratified and adopted the contract and the contract is warranted by the terms of the incorporation."
27. To affect and apprised the provisions of section 27(b) of the Act, we have carefully read out testimonies of all the DWs.

28. Gorangha Chandra Das, DW No.1 is a son of Kailash Chandra Das who in his testimonies stated nothing regarding the case of added defendant Nos. 5-7, nor stated that the added defendants purchased the land without the knowledge of the original Bainapatra. This witness straight way denied the Bainanama of his father Kailas Chandra Das although it was not proved concurrently before both the Court below. The High Court Division never tried to discuss the matter in the impugned judgment.
29. DW 2 Mahmud Ali in his testimony testified nothing about the Bainanama, in his denial stated that he had purchased in good faith without knowledge of the plaintiff's contract but such denial was not supported by any of the DWs and documentary evidence.
30. DW 3-Abdul Gani is scribe of Exhibits A, A(1), DW 4-Zahir Ali also did not testify about the facts of the Bainapathra, DW 5- Asaddar Ali in his testimonies nothing mentioned about earlier Bainapartha save and except denied the same saying that Bainamama is false, which means he knew about the facts of Bainanama, unless how say it is false. DW 6-Rashid Ali in his testimonies did not say anything about earlier Bainanama, rather, testified about the sell of the suit land and payment of consideration.
31. From those testimonies and discussions, there is no such assertion that they were purchasers of the said property paying the money in good faith and without notice of the original contract.
32. Mere denying the facts of original Bainanama in the written statement will not ipso facto acted upon, such, facts must be proved through oral and documentary evidence. Furthermore, to make applicable the provisions of section 27(b) of the Specific Relief Act i.e. bonafide transfer for value without notice, such plea of the subsequent transferee onus lies on him to prove absence of such notice.
33. So, this point raised by the learned senior Counsel for the added respondents do not come to help in the instant case.
34. Contrariwise, it is crystal clear from the testimony of l'W 8, Mr Tobarak Ali which runs as follows:
“......বিবাদী মাহমুদ আলীর জমির লাগা আমার জমি আছে। জমিতে আমি চাষ করেছিলাম এবং মাহমুদ তার ভাই আব্দুল আলীসহ জমিতে তাদের জমি চাষকরেছিল এমন সময় বিবাদী আছালুল্লার কাছে জমি জমা সম্বন্ধে কথাবার্তা বলছিল । আমি সেখানে গিয়ে কি কথা হচ্ছে জিজ্ঞেস করলে আছাদ্দর আহালুল্লার বাড়ীর দিকে নির্দেশ করে বলে আমরা এই জমি এতদিন ভাগী করছিলাম । এখন এ বাড়ীর লোক খরিদ করার চুক্তি করেছে।”
XXX: ১০/১২ বছর আগে কৈলাস মারা গিয়াছে সোলেমান চুক্তির কথা বলার সময় আর কেউ সেখানে ছিল না। বাড়ীর লোক আমার বাড়ী ৫/৭ দূরে এবং বিবাদীর বাড়ীর লাগোয়া । হারিমুদ্দেমের জমি অধিকারী । সে বাদীর ভাই। ৪নং বিবাদীর বিরুদ্ধে কয়েকদিন আগে মুন্সেফ কোর্টে সাক্ষী দিয়েছি । সত্য নহে যে, বিবাদীর সাথে শক্রতার জন্য মিথ্যা সাক্ষ্য দিয়েছি।
XXX: ৫ হইতে ৭: সকাল ৭/৮ টার সময় আছাদের সাথে কথা হয়েছিল বিবাদীরা তখনও আমি ছাড়া তখন কেউ ছিল না।
35. In cross the added defendants did not deny those testimonies of PW 8. Therefore, the testimonies of this PW deem to have been admitted by the added defendants.
36. PW 6-Abdul Gani testified that,
“কৈলাসকে চিনিতাম। বাদী বিবাদীকে চিনি। আছাদ্দর ও কুটির কাছে শুনেছি যে কৈলাস ও বাদীর মধ্যে বিক্রির কথা হয়েছে । ৭/৮ বছর আগে বায়নামা হয়েছিল বলে শুনেছি।
XXX: ১/২ কৈলাসের সামনে বায়নামায় কথা শুনেছি।
XXX: ৫ হইতে ৭: আছাদ্দর ও কুটি যখন আলাপ করে তখন আমি শুনেছি। কৃষি জমিতে এই আলাপ হয়েছে । মাস ও সাল মনে নাই ।”
37. PW 3-Md Soleman Hossain, son of Md Ahaullah testified amongst other that,
“........ Defdts. 5 to 7 had knowledge of the contract because they were bhagidars under Kailash in the year of the contract and I had talk with them about the contract. They made purchase with knowledge about the contract. There are collusive documents. They have created three documents because. I had litigation with them from long before the contract.............”

38. Thereafter, on behalf of cross of defendant Nos.5-7, this witness replied to the effect that,
“............ I had civil litigation with defdts.5 to 7. It was filed by my gr. father who died 15 years back after its disposal. We are not good term with defdts we are not in writing term with them. I had talk about the contract with Mahmud Ali in Bhadra, 1379 when I was working in my field to the east of suit dag No.6. My witness Abdul Gani disclosed the contract to him and thereafter he ascertained it from me.
About a week after this Asaddar knew about the contract from me. I disclosed about it when I was plaughing land. He was also plaughing land nearby. I disclosed about my talk with Asaddar to Abdul Gani on my way to Sylhet."
39. In cross the added defendants did not deny those testimonies of the PW 3-Soleman Hossain. Therefore, the testimony of PW 3 deem to have been admitted by the added defendants from which it is abundantly clear that the added defendants were aware about the original Bainanama of the plaintiffs. Thus, the submissions advanced on behalf of the added defendants by the learned Counsel devoid of merit.
40. It is divulged that the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division opined in the impugned judgment to the effect that " The Lower Appellate Court wrongly and illegally decreed the suit for execution of sale deed by the defendants No.1-3 the heirs of the original owner Koilash Chandra Das. The sale deed executed by the defendant Nos.1-3 in favour of the defendants No.5-7 remains untouched, unaffected because no cancellation was sought for in the prayer of the plaint. The contract for sale of immovable property under section 54 of the Transfer of Property Act does not create any right/interest in the property. It is a document merely creating a right to obtain another document. The plaintiff asked for relief in the alternative on a part with each other and after grant of one of such alternative relief he is not an aggrieved person who could carry the matter to this Court, specific performance be a equitable relief which have been refused in due exercise of desecration by the trial Court which is not liable to be interfered by the lower Appellate Court in view of conspicuous absence of any finding that the learned Trial Court excersied its discretion arbitrarily........ "
41. The above findings and opinion in the impugned judgment is not only misconceived, rather, the fundamental and inherent error because if the added defendants could not proved that they had bonafide purchasers for value who has paid his money in good faith and without notice of the original contract in that case, there is no necessity to sought any relief against the added defendants and their alleged deeds in question.
<u>42. Since, the suit was for specific perfor-mance of contract by dint of registered Bainanama, such registration itself deem to be not only created a right for registration of sale deed, rather, seems to be a notice for purchasing the same property, in such suit, there is no scope to convert the same as a suit for declaration and cancellation against the added defendants. Moreover, the principal defendants got the suit properties by inheritance from their predecessors deceased Kailash Chandra Das who made registered agreement of bainapatra with predecessors of the plaintiff in the 1379 BS and on 1379 BS Corresponding to 1973 AD and received the part payment of the consideration in his life time, before registration of the deeds in question of added defendants. However, added defendants purchased the suit properties after death of the Kailash Chandra Das from his heirs. Therefore, it is the settled maxim of the law that the added defendants ought to prove that they purchased the property without notice to original bainanama. From our discussions as above, we have already found that the added defendants have failed to prove their part. Therefore, the opinion and discussions of the trial Court and the High Court Division are erroneous and without any merit.</u>
43. Moreso, the added defendants steps into the shoes of the principal defendants, in such case, the maxim of law has settled many more years ago holding that specific performance of the contract can be enforced against either party or against any other party who claims title under the original party. In the case of Eazher Meah and others vs Shaher Banu and others reported in 49 DLR (AD) 85 wherein this Division held that—
"The proper form of decree is to direct specific performance of the contract between the vendor and the plaintiff and direct subsequent transferee to join in the conveyance so as to pass on the title which resides in him to the plaintiff in order to avoid all controversies."
44. In the case of Nurul Islam and others vs Jamila Khatun and others reported in 53 DLR (AD) 45 this Division held that—
"In a suit for specific performance of contract for sale of immovable property plaintiff is entitled to delivery of possession. A trespasser in the suit property is liable to be impleaded in the suit and evicted from the suit property to give effective relief to the plaintiff."
45. In the case of Lal Miah (Hajee) vs Nurul Amin and others reported in 57 DLR (AD) 64 this Division was held that—
"The expression "under him" is referable to clause (a) of section 27 i.e. either party to the contract. As the defendant No.2 had acquired title to the property as regard which defendant No.1 earlier entered into an agreement for sale with the plaintiffs and as defendant No.2 failed to establish that he purchased the property in good faith without notice of the original contract, the Court was correct in decreeing the suit against the defendants and in directing defendant No.2 to execute and register kabala in favour of the plaintiffs."
46. The High Court Division passed the impugned judgment and order against the settled principles of law without appreciating the case of the plaintiff that alternative prayer was withdrawn by the plaintiff amending the plaint on 19-6-1984 vide, order No.91 which was not challenged by the contesting defendants in the Higher Court and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division cannot be sustained in law.
47. Accordingly, we find merit in submissions of the learned Counsel for the appellants. The reasons elaborated above we find that the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division do call for interference.
48. Accordingly, this Civil Appeal is allowed without any order as to cost. The judgment and order of the High Court Division dated 26-11-2006 as well as judgment and decree of the Trial Court dated 27-6-1984 are set-aside and judgment and decree of the Appellate Court dated 27-4-1997 is hereby restored.
The principal defendants and added defendants are directed to join in the conveyance and register the same in the name of the plaintiffs. If, they failed to do so, within 90 days from the received of the direction of the trial Court, the plaintiffs would be entitled to have the conveyance paying rest of the consideration money through Court in accordance with law.
End.

full_judgment:
Obaidul Hassan, J: This civil appeal by leave granting order dated 10-5-2015 passed in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1820 of 2010 is directed against the judgment and decree dated 9-12-2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.3819 of 2000 making the Rule absolute reversing the judgment and decree dated 8-5-1995 passed by the learned Additional Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Sadar, Dinajpur in Other Class Suit No.561 of 1990 decreeing the suit.
2. The relevant facts necessary for the disposal of this civil appeal are that the predecessor of the appellants namely Durga Mohan Roy as plaintiff instituted the above mentioned suit impleading the respondent No.1 and three others as defendants No.1-4 for recovery of Khas possession of the suit land by way of eviction under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877. The case of the plaintiff, in a nutshell, is that the land measuring 15 decimals appertaining to CS Plot No.599 and 20 decimals appertaining to CS Plot No.1013 under Balubari and Pran Nath Pur Mouza of Sadar Upazila, Dinajpur belonged to CS recorded tenants named Nirmal Chandra Roy, Jogodish Chandra Roy and others. On the demise of Nirmal Chandra Roy his share devolved upon his son Mrinal Chandra Roy, who sold 8 decimals land in the eastern part of the two suit plots to the plaintiff by a registered Kabala dated 14-1-1961. The plaintiff erected a house on the said 8 decimals land and started living thereon with his family. The other CS recorded tenant namely Jogodish Roy agreed to sell to the plaintiff another 13 decimal land out of the two suit plots by an unregistered Bainapatra in the year 1962 and delivered possession of the same. The plaintiff remained in possession of the said 21 decimal lands on the basis of the said Kabala and paid ground rent to the government. However, the sale deed was not ultimately executed by Jogodish Roy pursuant to the Bainapatra in respect of the 13 decimal land. But the plaintiff continued to be in possession of the said 13 decimal land contiguous to his purchased 8 decimal land. The unregistered Bainapatra was lost during the war of liberation. The fact of plaintiff's acquisition of and possession over 21 decimal land was admitted in two previous suits instituted by Jogodish Roy namely Other Class Suit No.271 of 1968 (for short 1st suit) and Partition Suit No.150 of 1983 (for short 2nd suit). In the first suit Jogodish Roy impleaded the plaintiff (deceased Durga Mohan) as defendant No.11, who filed a written statement, but subsequently Jogodish Roy excluded toe plaintiff from the suit and thereby admitted latter's possession over the suit land. Later on the first suit was withdrawn by Jogodish. In the second suit Jogodish again impleaded the plaintiff as defendant No.1 and admitted his possession. However, that suit was abated. In the night following 13-3-1989 and in the morning of 14-3-1989 the present defendant No.1, Belly Khatoon dispossessed the plaintiff i.e. deceased Durga Mohan from the suit land measuring 12½ decimal by erecting a small room along with bamboo fence with the help of some local unruly people. The defendant No.1 also created a false deed of Heba-bil-Ewaz dated 26-4-1989. The said deed was purportedly executed by Mrinal Kanti alias Yusuf in favour of his wife, the defendant No.l. But in fact Mrinal Kanti being the son of the recorded tenant Nirmal Roy died much before 26-4-1989 and he was neither married to defendant No.1 nor did he convert himself as a Muslim. The plaintiff requested the defendant No.1 to vacate the suit land but she refused. Hence the suit.
3. The defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint. She contended, inter alia, that the suit is bad for defect of parties, barred by limitation and not maintainable. Nirmal Roy and Jogodish Roy were the CS recorded tenants along with 3 other co-sharers namely Jatindra Kishore, Purnendu Kishore and Sharodindu Roy. The share of Nirmal Roy devolved upon his son Mrinal Kanti Roy, who sold 8 decimals land out of the two suit plots to the plaintiff and the plaintiff had been in possession of that 8 decimal land only. Purnendu and Sharodindu died leaving no issue and their shares devolved upon their nephew Mrinal Kanti Roy. During his life-time said Mrinal Kanti Roy used to possess the lands of suit plots in Ejmali with Jogodish Chandra. Thereafter said Mrinal Kanti Roy embraced Islam and adopted the name of Yusouf Ali and married the defendant No.1. Subsequently, the share of Jogodish Roy also devolved upon his cousin Mrinal Kanti Roy. In the following way, the husband of the defendant No.1 namely Mrinal Kanti Roy had been in continuous possession of 13¼ decimal land in the two suit plots and used to run a wood shop in the name and style 'M/s Beauty Rany Roy' up to the year 1987. Mrinal Kanti Roy also erected a house on the suit land and used to live hi that house with the defendant No.1. The husband of the defendant No.1 transferred 8 decimals land in the said two plots to the plaintiff by registered sale deed dated 18-1-1961. Said Mrinal Kanti Roy transferred 13¼ decimal land appertaining to plots No.599 and 1013 to the defendant No.1 by a registered deed of Hiba-bil-Ewaz dated 26-4-1989. The defendant No.1 had been possessing 13¼ decimal land in the said two plots. The plaintiff has no title and possession in the land of suit plots except 8 decimal land. Apart from the defendant No.1 other co-sharers are in possession of the rest partition of the land of suit plots. The plaintiff had not acquired any title and possession in pursuant to the alleged deed of agreement from Jogodish Chandra Roy. In Partition Suit No.3 of 1974 Mrinal Kanti alias Yusuf Ali was defendant No.1 and in that suit an order of injunction was passed at the instance of Mrinal Kanti in his favour restraining other defendants including the plaintiff, who was defendant No.11 from interfering with his possession in respect of 26¼ decimal land of the suit plots and, as such, the possession of Mrinal Kanti over the suit land was intact and after his death his wife namely the defendant No.1 is in possession of the same and, as such, the plaintiff having no possession in the suit land and, as such, the instant suit is liable to be dismissed.
4. During the trial of the case, the trial Court framed six issues for disposal of the suit. The plaintiff examined four witnesses as PWs 1-4 while the defendant No.1 also examined four witnesses as DWs 1-4. Both the parties adduced documentary evidences in support of their respective case.
5. The trial Court on completion of the trial decreed the suit in part by judgment and decree dated 8-5-1995. Being aggrieved by the judgment of the trial Court the defendant No.1 filed Civil Revision No.3819 of 2000 before the High Court Division against the judgment and decree dated 8-5-1995 passed by the trial Court and Rule was issued.
6. Upon final hearing, the High Court Division was pleased to make the Rule absolute by judgment and decree dated 9-12-2009.
7. Being disgruntled with the judgment and decree dated 9-12-2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3819 of 2000 the successors of the plaintiff preferred the Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1820 of 2010 before this Division and after hearing this Division was pleased to grant leave on 10-5-2015 and hence the instant appeal.
8. In the said Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1820 of 2010 the leave was granted on the following points:
I. For that the instant suit is for recovery of Khas possession under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act and cardinal question is whether before dispossession, the plaintiff was in possession or not and the suit has been filed within 6 months from the date of dispossession and the High Court Division committed an error in travelling beyond the scope of the suit by discussing the title of the parties.
II. For that in the plaint of Title Suit No.150 of 1983 the plaintiff of that suit Jogodish Chandra Roy admitted in paragraph-3 of the plaint that plaintiff and defendant No.1 (the present plaintiff) have been possessing the land in question and Jogodish did not say about possession of Mrinal Kanti and he further stated that "কালক্রমে ঘেরা বেড়া নষ্ট হয়ে যাওয়ায় ১নং বিবাদী অসৎ উদ্দেশ্যে বাদীর আতাতে বিনা মাপে নতুন ঘেরা বেড়া দিয়া দাগের অধিকাংশ ভূমিতে বৃক্ষাদি রোপন করিতেছেন।" which indicates the possession of Durga Mohan and he claimed his possession by filing written statement over 11 decimals out of 20 decimals from plot No.1013, 10 decimals out of 15 decimals from plot No.599 and in total 21 decimals, from that land 13 decimals is the suit land and Mrinal Kanti also admitted possession of the present plaintiff in his written statement, but the High Court Division committed an error that the plaintiff has failed to prove his possession and dispossession.
9. Mr Bivash Chandra Biswas, learned Advocate-on-record, appearing on behalf of the appellants taking us through the judgment and decree of the High Court Division dated 9-12-2009 passed in Civil Revision No.3819 of 2000, judgment and decree of the trial Court, the other materials on record, contends that the High Court Division has committed illegality in totally misconceiving the case of the appellant upon misreading and misconstruing the evidence and materials on record and thereby misdirected beyond the law and facts of the case in passing the erroneous judgment making the Rule absolute occasioning serious mis-carriage of justice and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set-aside. The learned Counsel contends further that in suit for recovery of Khas possession under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act the cardinal question necessary to be considered as to whether the plaintiff was in possession of the suit land prior to the dispossession and filed the suit within 6(six) months from the date of dispossession. The learned Counsel contends further that although the possession of the plaintiff is admitted by the defendant, the High Court Division could not appreciate the matter and most illegally set-aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court and, as such, the judgment and decree of the High Court Division is liable to be set-aside.
10. In opposition, none appears on behalf of the respondents.
11. We have perused the judgment and decree dated 9-12-2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3819 of 2000. We have also considered the submissions of the learned Counsel for the appellants and gone through the judgment and decree of the trial Court, evidences and other materials on record.
12. On scrutiny of the record, it transpires that the predecessor of the appellants namely Durga Mohan Roy as plaintiff instituted the suit for recovery of Khas possession of the suit land by way of eviction under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 impleading the respondent No.1 and three others as defendants No.1-4.
13. It has been held by this Division in the case of Yakub Ali (Md) vs Md Attar Rahman and others reported in 4 BLC (AD) 149, Paragraph-9 that—
"All that a plaintiff in a suit under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act is required to prove is his possession and dispossession within 6(six) months next before the institution of the suit. The trial Court factually found the possession and dispossession of the plaintiff from the disputed land within the specified period. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division found no error of law in the said finding. In a suit of this nature the court is quite competent to pass a decree in favour of the plaintiff for recovery of possession of the suit land, notwithstanding any claim of title that may be set up in defence. We, therefore, find no merit in the contention."
14. It has also been held in the case of Ziaraf Hossain (Md) vs Md Jaher Ali and others, reported in 59 DLR (AD) 153 Paragraph-4 that—
“.......... the High Court Division further found that in order to succeed in a case under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act the plaintiff has to prove his possession of the suit land prior to dispossession as alleged in the plaint and also that the suit was filed within 6(six) months from the date of dispossession, but in the instant case the plaintiff failed to prove his possession of the suit land prior to forcible dispossession by the defendants on 15-10-1998. Accordingly, the High Court Division made the Rule absolute."
15. Again, section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 laid down in the following:
"9. Suit by person dispossessed of immoveable property—If any person is dispossessed without his consent of immoveable property otherwise than in due course of law, he or any person claiming through him may, by suit recover possession thereof, notwithstanding any other title that may be set up in such suit."
<u>16. In view of the provisions of law as well as the judicial pronouncement made by this Division it is settled law that in a suit for recovery of Khas possession under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 the moot question necessary to be decided as to whether the plaintiff had possession prior to forceful dispossession from the suit land. Now let us see how far the plaintiff has been able to prove his possession in the suit land prior to dispossession.</u>
17. On scrutiny of the record it appears that the plaintiff filed the necessary documents of the Partition Suit No.150 of 1983 which had been marked as Exhibit 4 series. In the Plaint of Suit No.150 of 1983 the plaintiff of that suit Jogodish Chandra Roy admitted in paragraph-3 of the plaint that (he) plaintiff and defendant No.1 (the present plaintiff) have been possessing the land in question and Jogodish did not say about possession of Mrinal Kanti. Said Jogodish Chandra Roy further stated that—" কালক্রমে ঘেরা বেড়া নষ্ট হয়ে যাওয়ায় ১নং বিবাদী অসৎ উদ্দেশ্যে বাদীর আতাতে বিনা মাপে নতুন ঘেরা বেড়া দিয়া দাগের অধিকাংশ ভূমিতে বৃক্ষাদি রোপন করিতেছেন। "
18. The said statement supports the possession of Durga Mohan and he claimed his possession by filing written statement over 11 decimals from plot No.1013 and 10 decimals from plot No.599 totaling 21 decimals and out of the said land that land 13 decimals is the suit land and Mrinal Kanti also admitted the possession of the present plaintiff in his written statement, but the High Court Division committed an error that the plaintiff has failed to prove his possession and dispossession in the suit land.
19. In the light of the foregoing discussion it is evident that the plaintiff has been able to prove his possession prior to his dispossession from the suit land. The trial Court on proper appreciation of the facts and law lawfully decreed the suit, but the High Court Division most illegally set-aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court.
20. In view of the aforesaid reasons, the impugned judgment and decree of the High Court Division warrants interference by this Division. Therefore, we find merit in the submissions of the learned Counsel for the appellants. In the prevailing circumstances, the impugned judgment and decree of the High Court Division cannot stand at all in the eye of law.
21. Accordingly, the instant civil appeal is allowed.
The judgment and decree dated 9-12-2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.3819 of 2000 is hereby set-aside.
End.

Mr. M.I Farooqui, Senior Advocate with Ms. Nazneen Nahar, Advocate (Appearing Virtually) ------- For the petitioner.
Mr. Hasan Tareq, Advocate (Appearing Virtually) --------- For the opposite party No.1-4 & 6.
